definition_zh: 物质；事情；问题；要紧、有关系；【医】脓液
definition_en: the physical stuff that things are made of, an affair under discussion, or to be important
core_image: 一块被雨水泡软的黑泥，手指一捏就能变形，也能弄脏任何碰到它的东西
scene: 泥地刚被雨水浸透，脚一踩就陷下去，鞋底带起黏稠的一团。The sticky mud is the matter that stains every boot in the yard.
sceneCN: 这里 matter 指构成物体的有形之物（第 1 个义项：与形式相对、可被感官触及的实体材料）；句意：那团黏泥就是弄脏院子里每只靴子的物质。图中可辨识物件：泥洼、沾泥的靴子、铁锹、水桶。

pos.zh: 物质；事情；问题；脓液
要紧；有重大关系

forms.label: 单数（物质义通常不可数）

derivatives.zh: 就事论事的；不动声色的（由本词与「事实」一词构成的复合形容词）
反物质（加表示「相反」的前缀构成，指电荷相反的物质）
无实质内容的（加表示「没有」的后缀构成）
含脓的（加形容词后缀构成，旧医学用法，现已罕用）

senses.title: Physical substance
senses.definition: the physical substance that occupies space and can be seen or touched
senses.definitionCN: 占据空间、可被看见或摸到的实体材料
senses.example: The sticky mud is the matter that stains every boot in the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 那团黏泥就是弄脏院子里每只靴子的物质。
senses.why: matter goes back to Latin materia, which meant timber and the stuff a thing is built from, so the physical sense is the oldest layer.
senses.whyCN: matter 上溯到拉丁 materia，本指木料与造物所用的料，因此「有形之物」是最古老的一层意思。

senses.title: An affair or business
senses.titleCN: 一件待办或已办的事情
senses.definition: a situation, event or piece of business that someone deals with
senses.definitionCN: 某人需要处理的情境、事件或事务
senses.example: She settled a few private matters before leaving for the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 去海边之前，她先处理了几件私事。
senses.why: Latin materia also named the subject under discussion, so the stuff of a talk became the affair itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 materia 也指谈论的题目，于是「谈话的料」就变成了「事情本身」。

senses.title: A problem to be solved
senses.titleCN: 出了差错、需要弄清的问题
senses.definition: a trouble or difficulty, especially one whose cause is not yet known
senses.definitionCN: 麻烦或困难，尤指原因尚未查明的那一种
senses.example: The mechanic asked what the matter was with the engine.
senses.exampleCN: 修理工问发动机出了什么毛病。
senses.why: an affair that has gone wrong is still an affair, so the same word shifted from business to trouble.
senses.whyCN: 出了岔子的事情仍然是一件事情，这个词便从「事务」滑到「麻烦」。

senses.title: To be important
senses.definition: to be of importance or consequence to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某事具有重要性或后果
senses.example: Accuracy matters more than speed in this laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 在这间实验室里，准确比速度更要紧。
senses.why: what has substance has weight, and English turned that picture into the verb sense of counting for something.
senses.whyCN: 有实体就有分量，英语把这个画面变成了「算得上数」的动词义。

senses.title: The topic of a text or talk
senses.definition: the subject or content that a piece of writing, speech or study is about
senses.definitionCN: 一篇文章、一段讲话或一项研究所谈论的主题与内容
senses.example: The matter of the lecture was soil chemistry in dry regions.
senses.exampleCN: 那场讲座的主题是干旱地区的土壤化学。
senses.why: the material of a text is what it carries, and that carrying sense became the topic it treats.
senses.whyCN: 文章的「料」就是它所承载的东西，这一承载义再转为它所处理的主题。

senses.title: Grounds for concern
senses.titleCN: 值得忧虑或申诉的根据
senses.definition: a reason or grounds for a feeling, claim or action
senses.definitionCN: 某种情绪、主张或行动的根据与理由
senses.example: The inspectors found matter for concern in the water samples.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员在采水样中发现了值得忧虑的情况。
senses.why: a matter is something that exists and can be pointed at, so it came to mean a fact solid enough to base a claim on.
senses.whyCN: 事情是存在且指得出的事物，于是引申为「站得住脚、可作依据的事实」。

senses.title: Pus from a wound
senses.definition: the fluid that forms in an infected wound, formerly called matter
senses.definitionCN: 感染伤口中生成的液体，旧时称作 matter
senses.example: The old surgical notes describe the wound discharging matter.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的手术记录描述伤口流出脓液。
senses.why: early medicine used matter for any fluid substance of the body, and pus was simply the matter a wound produced.
senses.whyCN: 早期医学用 matter 泛指体内各种液体，脓不过是伤口生成的「物质」。

senses.title: Content as opposed to form
senses.titleCN: 与形式相对的实质内容
senses.definition: the substantive content of a work, as distinct from its style or outward form
senses.definitionCN: 作品的实际内容，与风格或外在形式相对
senses.example: The matter of the essay outweighs its elegant phrasing.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇随笔的内容比它漂亮的措辞更有分量。
senses.why: philosophy opposed matter to form, and literary criticism then asked whether a work had matter behind its shape.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把「质料」与「形式」对举，文学批评随后追问一部作品在形之外有没有实质。

intro.en: Matter came into English through Old French from Latin materia 'timber, stuff, subject'. The common claim that materia derives from mater 'mother' is a hypothesis, not a settled derivation.
intro.cn: matter 经古法语来自拉丁 materia「木料、材料、题目」。常有人说 materia 由 mater「母亲」派生，那是假说，并非已定的词源。

items.en: Materia meant timber and the material a thing is made from, and by extension the subject of a discussion.
items.cn: materia 指木料以及造物所用的材料，引申为谈论的题目。

items.en: A widely repeated suggestion links materia to mater 'mother', as if the stuff were the mother of the object; this remains a hypothesis and is not established.
items.cn: 一种广为流传的说法把 materia 与 mater「母亲」联系起来，仿佛材料是器物的母亲；这仍属假说，未获证实。

items.en: Old French matere carried both the physical sense and the sense of a subject or affair into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 matere 在诺曼时期之后把「物质」与「题目、事务」两义一并带入英语。

items.en: Middle English matter already covered stuff, a business, a question and grounds for complaint, so the wide sense range is old, not modern.
items.cn: 中古英语的 matter 已兼指物质、事务、问题与申诉的理由，可见义域之宽古已有之，并非现代才有。

items.en: Medical writing of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries used matter for bodily fluid and especially for pus, a use that has since narrowed.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪的医学文献用 matter 指体液，尤指脓，这一用法后来收窄。

items.en: The first recorded dates for several senses are approximate; the word itself is well attested from the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 若干义项的最早记录年代为约数；这个词本身在十三世纪已有充分书证。

note.en: The first group contains forms that look or sound close to matter but may sit on a different root; the second group contains words that share part of its meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是形或音与 matter 接近、但未必同源的词；第二组是与之部分同义的词。

entries.definition: Built on Latin materialis from materia, so it is the adjective and noun grown from the same stock as matter, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁 materialis 构成，而 materialis 出自 materia，因此它是与 matter 同出一源的名词与形容词，并非另一个词根。

entries.definition: A French-shaped doublet of material, borrowed later for military equipment and supplies; it shares the Latin source but not the everyday meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 是 material 的法语式借形词，后借入指军用装备与物资；与 material 同源，但日常义不同。

entries.definition: From Latin mater 'mother' through maternellus; it is related to mater, and only through the unproven mater-materia hypothesis could it be called a cousin of matter.
entries.definitionCN: 经 maternellus 出自拉丁 mater「母亲」；它与 mater 有关，只有借助尚未证实的「母亲—材料」假说，才能算作 matter 的远亲。

entries.definition: From Latin matrix 'womb, mould', built on mater; it names a mould or grid, and does not descend from materia.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 matrix「子宫、模具」，由 mater 构成；它指模具或网格，并非由 materia 传下。

entries.definition: Physical stuff considered as what stands under qualities; matter stresses the material, substance stresses independent existence.
entries.definitionCN: 把物质看作承载属性的基底；matter 强调材料，substance 强调独立存在。

entries.definition: A matter of business or public concern; it covers only the affair sense and never the physical one.
entries.definitionCN: 指事务或公众关注之事；只覆盖「事务」义，绝不指物质。

entries.definition: A topic on which people disagree; it is narrower than matter because it always implies debate.
entries.definitionCN: 指人们有分歧的议题；比 matter 窄，因为它总含争辩之意。

entries.definition: The everyday word for unspecified material; matter is its neutral and technical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指未指明材料的日常说法；matter 是它中性、技术化的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin source, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁来源、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin materia first meant timber, so matter is the stuff a thing is built from.
normal.cn: 拉丁 materia 最初指木料，因此 matter 就是造物所用的料。

normal.en: The family runs matter, material, materially, immaterial and materialize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 matter、material、materially、immaterial 与 materialize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the affair sense: a matter of time, as a matter of fact, no matter what.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出「事情」义：只是时间问题、事实上、无论发生什么。

normal.en: Subject matter keeps the topic sense visible in publishing and teaching.
normal.cn: 「主题素材」这一说法让「主题」义在出版与教学里一直可见。

normal.en: The verb is used in questions of value: it matters, it does not matter.
normal.cn: 动词义出现在价值判断里：这要紧、这不要紧。

abstract.en: Picture a lump of clay that takes the shape of whatever presses into it.
abstract.cn: 想象一团黏土，什么按上去就留下什么形状。

abstract.en: Picture a desk with one folded note on it, and everyone asks about that note first.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上只有一张折起的字条，所有人先问的都是那张字条。

abstract.en: Picture a scale where the pan with real goods sinks and the empty pan rises.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆秤，装了实物的那端沉下去，空的那端翘起来。

examples.en: In legal drafting, the matter of a contract means its operative content rather than its layout.
examples.cn: 在法律起草中，合同的 matter 指其有效内容，而不是排版。

examples.en: Dark matter does not emit light, yet its gravity holds galaxies together.
examples.cn: 暗物质不发光，但它的引力把星系维系在一起。

examples.en: It does not matter how slowly you go as long as the measurements stay exact.
examples.cn: 只要测量保持精确，你走得多慢都不要紧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「妈特」——妈妈特别在意的那件事，就是要紧的事 → 事情、要紧；妈妈捏的那团泥，就是物质

root: 拉丁 materia「木料、材料、题目」（一说由 mater「母亲」派生，仅为常见假说）→ 古法语 matere「材料、事务」→ 英语 matter；「问题」与「脓」义由「事情」「体内物质」再引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one lump of stuff: it is the material of things, then the material of talk, then the affair, the trouble inside it, the fact that carries weight, the topic of a text, the fluid in a wound, and finally content set against form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一团「料」辐射出去：先是造物的材料，再是谈话的材料，继而成为事情、事情里的麻烦、有分量的事实、文本的主题、伤口的液体，最后是与形式相对的实质内容。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lump of wet clay that can be shaped, weighed and pointed at.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团湿黏土，可被塑形、称重、指认。

branches.en: THE LUMP ITSELF: clay in the yard and pus in a wound are both stuff a body or a boot meets.
branches.cn: 这团东西本身：院里的泥与伤口的脓，都是身体或靴子会碰到的实体。

branches.en: THE AFFAIR AND ITS SNAG: business first, then the trouble discovered inside it.
branches.cn: 事情与其中的疙瘩：先是事务，再是事务里查出的麻烦。

branches.en: WEIGHT THAT COUNTS: what has substance can tip a decision, so matter becomes a verb.
branches.cn: 有分量才算数：有实体就能压动决定，于是 matter 变成动词。

branches.en: STUFF POINTED AT: the material of a text turns into its topic, and a solid fact into grounds.
branches.cn: 被指认的料：文本的材料变成主题，扎实的事实变成依据。

branches.en: CONTENT AGAINST FORM: philosophy keeps the lump as what remains when style is stripped away.
branches.cn: 内容对形式：哲学把那团料保留为剥去风格后剩下的东西。

intro.en: Matter is built on a Latin root that also yields material and immaterial, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: matter 建立在一个拉丁词根上，同一词根还生出 material 与 immaterial，因此这个词族可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin materia supplies matter, material and materialis; mater supplies maternal and matrix, with the materia link remaining a hypothesis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 materia 衍生 matter 与 material 一系；mater 衍生 maternal 与 matrix 一系，而 materia 与 mater 的联系仍属假说。

items.example: The root gives the picture of stuff a thing is built from.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根给出「造物所用之料」的画面。

items.example: Its link to materia is a hypothesis, not a proven derivation.
items.exampleCN: 它与 materia 的联系只是假说，并非已证的派生。

items.example: The adjective suffix turns stuff into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 形容词后缀把「料」变成描述性的词。

items.example: Material keeps both the physical and the serious sense.
items.exampleCN: material 兼有「物质」与「重要」两义。

items.example: It also shapes editorial and commercial.
items.exampleCN: 它同样构成 editorial 与 commercial。

items.example: The negation covers both the physical and the serious sense.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀同时否掉「物质」与「重要」两义。

items.example: The plan materialized as a real building.
items.exampleCN: 计划落实成了一座真实的建筑。

items.example: The later borrowing narrowed to army supplies.
items.exampleCN: 后借入的这一形收窄为军队物资。

definition_zh: 材料；原料；布料；素材、资料；物质的；重要的、实质性的
definition_en: the stuff from which something is made, cloth, facts used for a work, or being important and physical
core_image: 一匹摊在裁床上的灰蓝布料，剪刀沿粉线往里走，布屑落在木台上
scene: 裁床上的灰蓝布料摊开，剪刀沿粉线往里走，布屑落了一地。The tailor spreads the material and cuts along the chalk line.
sceneCN: 这里 material 指可裁剪缝制的织物（第 2 个义项：做衣服用的布料）；句意：裁缝把布料铺开，沿着粉线裁剪。图中可辨识物件：裁床、灰蓝布料、剪刀、粉线。

pos.zh: 材料；原料；布料；素材、资料
物质的；重要的、实质性的

forms.label: 单数（物质义通常不可数）
复数（指多种材料或布料）

derivatives.zh: 唯物主义者；追逐物质的人

senses.title: Stuff used to build or make
senses.titleCN: 用来建造或制作的材料
senses.definition: the substance out of which something is made or built
senses.definitionCN: 用来制造或建造某物的物质
senses.example: Bricks and timber were the material of the old bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 砖与木料是这座老桥的材料。
senses.why: Late Latin materialis was simply the adjective of materia 'stuff', so the noun kept the plain sense of the stuff itself.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁 materialis 就是 materia「材料」的形容词，名词义因此保留了「料本身」这层直白意思。

senses.title: Cloth for sewing
senses.definition: fabric used for making clothes or furnishings
senses.definitionCN: 用来做衣服或家居用品的布料
senses.example: The tailor spread the material and cut along the chalk line.
senses.exampleCN: 裁缝把布料铺开，沿粉线裁剪。
senses.why: cloth was the material a household handled most often, so the word narrowed to fabric in everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 布料是家庭最常打交道的材料，于是这个词在日常口语中收窄为「织物」。

senses.title: Facts and sources for a work
senses.definition: information, notes or sources used for writing, research or a report
senses.definitionCN: 用于写作、研究或报道的信息、笔记与来源
senses.example: The reporter gathered material for the story over three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 记者用三周时间为这篇报道收集素材。
senses.why: what clay is to a pot, notes are to an article, so the same word covers the raw stuff of a text.
senses.whyCN: 黏土之于陶罐，正如笔记之于文章，于是同一个词也指文本的原料。

senses.title: Supplies and equipment
senses.definition: the things needed for a particular activity, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动所需的物品，通常用复数
senses.example: The laboratory ordered its materials for the autumn term.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室订购了秋季学期要用的用品。
senses.why: in the plural the word counts separate items rather than an uncountable stuff, a shift English makes freely with substances.
senses.whyCN: 复数把不可数的「料」转成一件件可数的东西，英语对物质名词常有这种转换。

senses.title: Physical rather than spiritual
senses.titleCN: 物质层面的，与精神相对
senses.definition: belonging to the physical world rather than to thought or spirit
senses.definitionCN: 属于物理世界，而非思想或精神世界
senses.example: The material world still obeys physical law.
senses.exampleCN: 物质世界依然服从物理规律。
senses.why: the adjective kept the old opposition of stuff to spirit, so it describes whatever can be touched.
senses.whyCN: 形容词保留了「材料对精神」的古老对举，因此描述一切摸得着的东西。

senses.title: Important to a decision
senses.definition: significant enough to affect a decision, a contract or a judgment
senses.definitionCN: 重要到足以影响决定、合同或判断的
senses.example: The delay was material to the terms of the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误对合同条款有实质影响。
senses.why: law and accounting borrowed the word because a fact with real stuff in it can change an outcome.
senses.whyCN: 法律与会计借用这个词，因为有实体内容的事实才足以改变结果。

senses.title: Concerned with wealth
senses.definition: interested in money and possessions rather than in higher aims
senses.definitionCN: 看重金钱与财物而非更高追求
senses.example: They chased material gain and ignored the damage.
senses.exampleCN: 他们追逐物质利益，无视造成的损害。
senses.why: if the material world is what can be touched, then gain in that world is money and goods.
senses.whyCN: 既然物质世界就是摸得着的那一面，那么那一面的收获自然就是钱与物。

senses.title: A person suited to a role
senses.definition: a person considered as suitable raw stuff for a particular post or task
senses.definitionCN: 被看作适合某项职位或任务的「生料」
senses.example: She is good material for the debate team.
senses.exampleCN: 她是辩论队的好苗子。
senses.why: a person is treated as raw stuff to be shaped by training, which keeps the oldest sense of material alive in a comic way.
senses.whyCN: 人被当成可被训练塑造的生料，这以略带戏谑的方式保留了 material 最古老的意思。

intro.en: Material is Late Latin materialis, the adjective of materia 'stuff', which passed through Old French into English. Its parent noun is the same source as matter.
intro.cn: material 是晚期拉丁 materialis，即 materia「材料」的形容词，经古法语进入英语；其母名词与 matter 同源。

items.en: Materia meant timber, stuff and subject matter; the adjective materialis was formed on it in later Latin.
items.cn: materia 指木料、材料与题材；形容词 materialis 是晚期拉丁语在它之上构成的。

items.en: Materialis meant 'of matter, physical' and was used in philosophy to contrast the physical with the spiritual.
items.cn: materialis 意为「物质的、物理的」，在哲学中用来与精神相对。

items.en: Old French material brought the adjective and noun into English in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries.
items.cn: 古法语 material 在十三、十四世纪把这个形容词与名词带入英语。

items.en: By the sixteenth century material was the ordinary word for cloth in a household, a sense that still survives in tailoring.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，material 已是家庭里指布料的常用词，这一义至今留在裁缝行当。

items.en: Modern law and accounting use 'material' for facts that can shift a decision, an extension of the idea of having real substance.
items.cn: 现代法律与会计用 material 指能改变决定的事实，这是「有实质」这一想法的延伸。

items.en: First recorded dates for the cloth, legal and accounting senses are approximate; the core adjective is well attested from the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 布料义、法律义与会计义的最早记录年代为约数；核心形容词义在十四世纪已有充分书证。

note.en: The first group holds near-forms of material, some sharing its Latin stock and some not; the second group holds words that overlap in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是与 material 形近的词，有的同出拉丁词源，有的不是；第二组是词义部分重叠的词。

entries.definition: The noun and verb built directly on materia; material is its learned adjective, so the two share a root but not a part of speech.
entries.definitionCN: 直接由 materia 构成的名词与动词；material 是它的书面形容词，二者同根而词性不同。

entries.definition: The same word borrowed a second time from French and narrowed to military stores; it is not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词第二次从法语借入，收窄为军用物资；并非另一个词根。

entries.definition: From mater 'mother', not materia; any family resemblance rests on the unproven mater-materia hypothesis.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 mater「母亲」而非 materia；所谓亲缘只建立在那条未获证实的假说上。

entries.definition: The adverb of material, used for 'to a significant degree'; it is a derived form, not a separate word.
entries.definitionCN: material 的副词，表示「达到显著程度」；它是派生形式，不是另一个词。

entries.definition: Material seen as the thing that underlies qualities; substance is more abstract and less countable.
entries.definitionCN: 被看作承载属性的材料；substance 更抽象、更不可数。

entries.definition: Cloth made by weaving; it covers only the textile sense of material.
entries.definitionCN: 织成的布；只覆盖 material 的织物义。

entries.definition: One of the substances combined in a mixture; material is the broader word for what anything is made of.
entries.definitionCN: 混合物中的一种成分；material 是更宽泛的「造物之料」。

entries.definition: Facts that support a conclusion; it overlaps the legal sense of material but not the sense of source material.
entries.definitionCN: 支持结论的事实；与 material 的法律义部分重叠，但不指写作素材。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin source, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁来源、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Materialis is the Latin adjective of materia, so material is literally 'of stuff'.
normal.cn: materialis 是 materia 的拉丁形容词，因此 material 字面上就是「属于材料的」。

normal.en: The family runs material, materially, materiality, materialism and materialize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 material、materially、materiality、materialism 与 materialize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physical sense: raw material, building material, material world.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物质义：原材料、建筑材料、物质世界。

normal.en: In law, a material fact is one that can change the outcome.
normal.cn: 在法律里，具有实质性的关键事实才能改变结果。

normal.en: The same Latin stock gives matter, and material is its adjective.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁词源也给出 matter，而 material 是它的形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a cutting table where the cloth decides what the coat can become.
abstract.cn: 想象一张裁床，布料本身决定了这件外套能做成什么样。

abstract.en: Picture a potter's hands choosing clay before any shape is attempted.
abstract.cn: 想象陶匠在动手塑形之前先挑泥料。

abstract.en: Picture a folder of notes that a writer keeps beside the blank page.
abstract.cn: 想象作家把一叠笔记放在空白稿纸旁边。

examples.en: Recycled material now accounts for a third of the plant's input.
examples.cn: 回收材料现在占这家工厂投入的三分之一。

examples.en: The committee judged the omission material to the audit.
examples.cn: 委员会认定这处遗漏对审计有实质影响。

examples.en: Course material is posted online before each lecture.
examples.cn: 课程材料在每次讲课前发布到网上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「买铁料」——盖房装修先买铁、买料，买的都是材料 → 材料、原料

root: 拉丁 materia「材料、木料」→ 晚期拉丁 materialis（materia 加形容词后缀）「物质的」→ 古法语 material → 英语 material；「布料」「重要」义由「做成东西的料」再引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all treat something as the stuff a thing is made from: bricks for a bridge, cloth for a coat, notes for a story, supplies for a term, the physical world for the spirit, facts for a decision, money for a life, and a person for a post.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某物当作「造物之料」：桥的砖、外套的布、报道的笔记、学期的用品、对抗精神的物质世界、影响决定的实据、支撑生活的钱财，以及适合某职位的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cloth on a cutting table, waiting to become something else.
core.cn: 核心意象：裁床上的一匹布，等着被做成别的什么。

branches.en: THE STOCK ITSELF: raw stuff in bulk, and the same stuff counted out as supplies for a term.
branches.cn: 原料本身：成批的生料，以及按学期点清的同一种用品。

branches.en: THE CLOTH ON THE TABLE: the material a household handles most often is fabric.
branches.cn: 桌上的那匹布：家庭最常打交道的材料就是织物。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL OF A TEXT: notes and sources are clay for a writer's pot.
branches.cn: 文本的料：笔记与来源是作家制陶的黏土。

branches.en: THE TOUCHABLE WORLD AND ITS GAINS: what can be touched, and what can be accumulated from it.
branches.cn: 可触摸的世界及其收获：摸得着的那一面，以及从那一面攒下的东西。

branches.en: STUFF THAT DECIDES: a fact with substance changes a contract, and a person with substance fills a post.
branches.cn: 起决定作用的料：有实质的事实能改动合同，有实质的人能补上职位。

intro.en: Material is one Latin root plus one adjective suffix, and both parts recur across a large English family.
intro.cn: material 由一个拉丁词根加一个形容词后缀构成，这两部分在英语的一大批词里反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin materia gives matter and material; the suffix -alis, through French -al, also shapes manual, editorial and commercial.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 materia 衍生 matter 与 material；后缀 -alis 经法语 -al 也构成 manual、editorial 与 commercial。

items.example: The root supplies the picture of raw stuff.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「生料」的画面。

items.example: The suffix makes an adjective of stuff.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把「材料」变成形容词。

items.example: Material carries both the physical and the serious sense.
items.exampleCN: material 兼有物质与重要两义。

items.example: The same ending appears in manual and editorial.
items.exampleCN: 同一词尾出现在 manual 与 editorial 中。

items.meaning: the quality of being material or significant
items.example: Auditors test materiality before they test figures.
items.exampleCN: 审计师先判断重要性，再核对数字。

items.meaning: the belief that matter is all there is
items.meaningCN: 认为物质即一切的学说
items.example: The suffix turns a quality into a doctrine.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把一种性质变成一种主义。

items.example: The design materialized as a real bridge.
items.exampleCN: 设计落实成了一座真实的桥。

items.example: The prefix denies both the stuff and the weight.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀同时否掉「实体」与「分量」。

items.example: A second borrowing narrowed to army stores.
items.exampleCN: 第二次借入的形收窄为军队物资。

definition_zh: 物质；实质、要旨；重要性、分量；财产、资产；【哲】实体
definition_en: the real matter of which something consists, the essential point of it, or its solid worth
core_image: 一只陶碗扣在桌上，碗底那圈看不见的支撑把整个碗稳稳托住
scene: 清漆刷过之后，木头表面亮起来，可真正撑住椅子的仍是里面那层看不见的木料。A coat of varnish hides the substance beneath.
sceneCN: 这里 substance 指构成物体、可独立存在的实体材料（第 1 个义项：与表面属性相对的实在物质）；句意：一层清漆盖住了下面真正的木料。图中可辨识物件：刷子、清漆罐、木椅、砂纸。

pos.zh: 物质；实质；要旨；重要性；财产

forms.label: 单数（物质义通常不可数）

senses.title: Physical stuff that stands under qualities
senses.titleCN: 承载各种属性的实在物质
senses.definition: the material that makes up a thing and remains when its surface qualities are ignored
senses.definitionCN: 构成某物、忽略表面属性后仍然存在的材料
senses.example: A coat of varnish hides the substance beneath.
senses.exampleCN: 一层清漆盖住了下面真正的木料。
senses.why: substance is Latin substantia, from sub- 'under' plus stare 'to stand', literally what stands beneath what we see.
senses.whyCN: substance 出自拉丁 substantia，由 sub-「在下」加 stare「站立」构成，字面就是「站在可见之物下面的东西」。

senses.title: The essential point
senses.definition: the main point or central meaning of a statement, argument or proposal
senses.definitionCN: 陈述、论证或提议的主要论点与核心意思
senses.example: The substance of her argument fits in a single sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 她论证的要旨一句话就能说完。
senses.why: what stands under a long speech is the one point holding it up, so the word moved from physical support to logical support.
senses.whyCN: 支撑一段长话的东西就是那一个支点，于是这个词从「物理支撑」转到「逻辑支撑」。

senses.title: Solid worth or importance
senses.titleCN: 实实在在的分量与价值
senses.definition: real value or seriousness, as opposed to mere appearance or style
senses.definitionCN: 真实的价值或严肃性，与单纯的外表或风格相对
senses.example: The proposal has substance even if its wording is clumsy.
senses.exampleCN: 这份提案措辞笨拙，却有实实在在的分量。
senses.why: a thing with substance has body, and a claim with body can carry weight in a debate.
senses.whyCN: 有实体就有体积，有体积的主张在争论中才压得住。

senses.title: Wealth and property
senses.definition: the goods and property that a person owns, an older use still found in religious wording
senses.definitionCN: 一个人拥有的财物与产业，这一旧义仍见于宗教文本
senses.example: He lost his substance when the warehouse burned.
senses.exampleCN: 仓库烧毁时，他失去了全部家产。
senses.why: in older English a person's substance was the material that stood under the household, namely its goods.
senses.whyCN: 在早期英语里，一个人的 substance 就是撑起这个家的实物，也就是家产。

senses.title: An entity in philosophy
senses.titleCN: 哲学中独立自存的实体
senses.definition: a thing that exists in itself and supports qualities, as opposed to an attribute
senses.definitionCN: 自身独立存在并承载属性的事物，与属性相对
senses.example: Philosophers ask whether the mind is a substance.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家追问心灵是不是一种实体。
senses.why: the Latin word was taken into philosophy to name whatever remains when all qualities are stripped away.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词被哲学借去，命名剥去所有属性之后仍然剩下的那个东西。

senses.title: Content rather than form
senses.titleCN: 作品中与形式相对的内容
senses.definition: the content of a work of art or writing considered apart from its form
senses.definitionCN: 文艺作品中与其形式分开来看的内容
senses.example: The essay lacks substance though it reads smoothly.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇随笔读起来顺，内容却空。
senses.why: criticism borrowed the philosophical pair, so substance became what a work says as against how it says it.
senses.whyCN: 文艺批评借用了哲学上的那对概念，substance 于是指作品「说了什么」，与「怎么说」相对。

senses.title: A specific chemical or drug
senses.titleCN: 某一种具体的化学物质或药物
senses.definition: a particular material with known chemical properties, especially one handled under regulation
senses.definitionCN: 具有已知化学性质的某种具体材料，尤指受管制的种类
senses.example: The laboratory stores radioactive substances in a shielded room.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室把放射性物质存放在屏蔽室里。
senses.why: once chemistry could identify kinds of stuff, the general word for stuff was applied to each named kind.
senses.whyCN: 化学能辨认出具体的种类之后，泛指「东西」的词就被用到每一个具名的种类上。

senses.title: Body or thickness in food
senses.titleCN: 汤汁、食物里的厚度与稠度
senses.definition: the thickness or body of a liquid or dish, giving it a sense of weight in the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 液体或菜肴的浓稠度，使其在口中有分量感
senses.example: Simmer the broth until it gains substance.
senses.exampleCN: 把汤慢慢熬到有厚度为止。
senses.why: a liquid with body has stuff standing under its surface, which is the original picture applied to cooking.
senses.whyCN: 有厚度的汤就是表面之下有实体撑着，这正是原初那个画面用在烹饪上。

intro.en: Substance came through Old French from Latin substantia, built on sub- 'under' and stare 'to stand'. Its literal picture is something standing beneath what appears.
intro.cn: substance 经古法语来自拉丁 substantia，由 sub-「在下」与 stare「站立」构成，字面画面就是「站在可见之物下面的东西」。

items.en: Stare meant 'to stand, to remain in place', and it supplies the picture of something upright and steady.
items.cn: stare 意为「站立、留在原处」，提供「立着、稳稳不动」的画面。

items.en: Sub- 'under' plus stare made substare 'to stand under, to be present beneath', a verb of support rather than of existence.
items.cn: sub-「在下」加 stare 构成 substare「站在下面、在下方存在」，这是一个支撑的动词，而非存在的动词。

items.en: Substantia was the noun of that verb, used for the underlying reality of a thing as opposed to its changing qualities.
items.cn: substantia 是该动词的名词，指事物底层的实在，与不断变化的属性相对。

items.en: Old French substance carried the word into English in the thirteenth century, with both the physical and the essential-point senses.
items.cn: 古法语 substance 在十三世纪把这个词带入英语，兼有「物质」与「要旨」两义。

items.en: Medieval theology and later philosophy sharpened the word into a technical term for what remains when attributes are removed.
items.cn: 中世纪神学与后来的哲学把这个词磨成一个术语，指剥除属性后仍然剩下的东西。

items.en: The first dates for the philosophical and chemical uses are approximate; the general noun is well attested from the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 哲学义与化学义的最早年代为约数；这个一般名词在十三世纪已有充分书证。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same 'standing under' root, plus one near-form from a different root; the second group holds words that overlap in meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「站在下面」这一词根的词，另加一个来自别的词根但形近的词；第二组是词义部分重叠的词。

entries.definition: Built on substantia with an adjective suffix, meaning 'large, solid, real'; it describes rather than names the stuff.
entries.definitionCN: 在 substantia 上加形容词后缀构成，意为「大量的、结实的、真实的」；它描述而非命名那个实体。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'having independent existence or real importance'; it often contrasts with procedural.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「独立存在的、有实质重要性的」形容词，常与「程序性的」相对。

entries.definition: To give substance to a claim by supplying proof; the verb adds the act of making something stand.
entries.definitionCN: 通过提供证据使主张站得住；这个动词加了「使某物立起来」的动作。

entries.definition: From sub- plus stratum, where stratum comes from sternere 'to spread', so it means a layer spread underneath, not something standing under.
entries.definitionCN: 由 sub- 加 stratum 构成，而 stratum 出自 sternere「铺开」，因此指铺在下面的一层，而非立在下面的东西。

entries.definition: The plain word for physical stuff; substance adds the idea of standing under qualities.
entries.definitionCN: 指物质材料的朴素说法；substance 多一层「承载属性」的意思。

entries.definition: Stuff viewed as what something is made from; substance views it as what something is.
entries.definitionCN: 被看作「用来做某物」的料；substance 则把它看作「某物之所是」。

entries.definition: The set of features that make a thing what it is; substance can mean just the main point, which is looser.
entries.definitionCN: 使一物成为该物的一组特征；substance 也可只指要点，宽泛一些。

entries.definition: What a work or container holds; it matches substance only in the writing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 作品或容器所装之物；只在文章义上与 substance 相合。

entries.definition: The central point of a text, usually summarized; it is narrower than substance and less formal.
entries.definitionCN: 文本的中心要点，通常经过概括；比 substance 窄，也没那么正式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin morphemes, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁语素、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: sub- 'under' plus stare 'stand': substance is what stands under the surface.
normal.cn: sub-「在下」加 stare「站立」：substance 就是站在表面之下的东西。

normal.en: The family runs substance, substantial, substantive, substantiate and insubstantial.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 substance、substantial、substantive、substantiate 与 insubstantial。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the material sense: chemical substance, harmful substance, controlled substance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物质义：化学物质、有害物质、受管制药物。

normal.en: In substance is the adverbial phrase meaning 'in essence'.
normal.cn: 表示「实质上」的副词性说法，正由这个名词义而来。

normal.en: A person of substance is someone with real wealth or real weight.
normal.cn: 说一个人有真实家产或真实分量，用的正是这个词。

abstract.en: Picture a bowl upside down, its rim holding the whole weight quietly.
abstract.cn: 想象一只倒扣的碗，碗沿不出声地撑住全部分量。

abstract.en: Picture a long speech with one small stone underneath it, holding it up.
abstract.cn: 想象一段冗长的讲话，底下垫着一块小石头把它撑住。

abstract.en: Picture a soup that coats the spoon, thick enough to have body.
abstract.cn: 想象一勺能挂住勺背的汤，浓得有了厚度。

examples.en: The study found no harmful substance in the groundwater.
examples.cn: 这项研究在地下水里没有发现有害物质。

examples.en: Stripped of jargon, the substance of the report is a warning about soil loss.
examples.cn: 去掉术语之后，这份报告的要旨是对土壤流失的警告。

examples.en: Her claims about the compound lack substance and cannot be tested.
examples.cn: 她关于这种化合物的说法缺乏实据，也无法检验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「萨布斯坦斯」——萨布站（stance 联想「站立」）在下面，就是撑着表面之下的实体 → 物质、实质

root: 拉丁 stare「站立」→ sub-「在下」加 stare 构成 substare「站在下面」→ 名词 substantia「站在下面的东西、实体」→ 古法语 substance → 英语 substance；「要旨、重要性」由「支撑」义引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all come from one picture: something stands under a visible surface. It is the wood under varnish, the point under a speech, the worth under a style, the goods under a household, the entity under qualities, the content under form, the chemical under a label, and the body under a broth.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都出自同一个画面：有东西站在可见表面之下。它是清漆下的木料、讲话下的要点、风格下的价值、家宅下的财物、属性下的实体、形式下的内容、标签下的化学品、汤面下的厚度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bowl turned upside down, its hidden base holding everything steady.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只倒扣的碗，看不见的碗底把一切稳稳托住。

branches.en: THE STUFF UNDERNEATH: wood beneath varnish, and the named chemical kinds that chemistry can separate.
branches.cn: 底下的实体：清漆下的木料，以及化学能分辨出的各种具名物质。

branches.en: THE SUPPORTING POINT: a long argument reduced to the one sentence that holds it up.
branches.cn: 支撑的要点：一段长论证收束为把它撑住的那一句话。

branches.en: WEIGHT AND CONTENT: what gives a work value, and what remains when its form is stripped off.
branches.cn: 分量与内容：使作品有价值的东西，以及剥去形式后剩下的东西。

branches.en: PROPERTY AS SUBSTANCE: the goods that literally stood under an old household.
branches.cn: 作为实体的家产：早期家庭里真正撑起门户的那些财物。

branches.en: ENTITY AND BODY: what philosophy leaves after qualities, and what a thick broth leaves in the mouth.
branches.cn: 实体与厚度：哲学剥去属性后留下的东西，以及浓汤留在口里的分量。

intro.en: Substance is a Latin prefix plus a Latin verb, and the whole chain from stare to substantiate can be read piece by piece.
intro.cn: substance 由一个拉丁前缀加一个拉丁动词构成，从 stare 到 substantiate 的整条链都可以逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin stare also gives stable, station and statue; sub- gives submarine and subsoil; their union gives substance and its English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 stare 还衍生 stable、station 与 statue；sub- 见于 submarine 与 subsoil；二者结合给出 substance 及其英语词族。

items.example: The prefix places the support below what is seen.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把支撑放到可见之物下面。

items.example: The root supplies the upright, steady picture.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「立着不动」的画面。

items.structure: sub- plus stare, as a noun
items.example: The noun turns the support into a thing.
items.exampleCN: 名词化把那层支撑变成一件东西。

items.example: Substance keeps both the physical and the essential sense.
items.exampleCN: substance 兼有物质与实质两义。

items.example: A substantial meal has body to it.
items.exampleCN: 一顿丰盛的饭有实在的分量。

items.example: Substantive talks deal with content, not schedule.
items.exampleCN: 实质性会谈谈内容，不谈日程。

items.example: The verb makes a claim stand on solid ground.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词使主张立在坚实的根基上。

items.example: The negation removes the body from the thing.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀把那层实体抽走。

latinEntries.meaning: to stand under; to be present

definition_en: a large shapeless body of matter, a great quantity of it, or the amount of matter in a body
core_image: 一盆揉好的面团被两只手按下去，整团摊在案板上，越揉越沉
scene: 面粉加水和成一大团，摊在案板上占了半张台面，两只手按下去要费点力。A mass of dough filled the whole board.
sceneCN: 这里 mass 指没有定形、聚成整体的一大团东西（第 1 个义项：不分形状的团块）；句意：一大团面团占满了整块案板。图中可辨识物件：面团、案板、面粉袋、擀面杖。

pos.zh: 团块；大量；质量；群众；弥撒
大规模的；大批的
聚集；集结

senses.title: A shapeless lump
senses.definition: a body of matter with no clear shape, often formed by pressing things together
senses.definitionCN: 没有明确形状的一团物质，常由挤压而成
senses.example: A mass of dough filled the whole board.
senses.exampleCN: 一大团面团占满了整块案板。
senses.why: Latin massa meant a lump of dough or metal, so the shapeless lump is the root picture of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 massa 指面团或金属的一团，因此「无定形的一团」是这个词的根源画面。

senses.title: A very large quantity
senses.definition: a great number or amount of things taken together
senses.definitionCN: 许多事物合在一起所形成的大数量
senses.example: A mass of evidence supports the claim.
senses.exampleCN: 大量证据支持这一主张。
senses.why: a lump is many small pieces pressed into one, so the word naturally shifted from one lump to a heap of things.
senses.whyCN: 一团是许多小块压在一起，于是这个词自然从「一团」滑到「一堆」。

senses.title: Quantity of matter in physics
senses.definition: the quantity of matter in a body, measured by its resistance to acceleration
senses.definitionCN: 物体所含物质的量，以其抵抗加速度的程度来量度
senses.example: Mass is not the same as weight, though scales blur the two.
senses.exampleCN: 质量与重量并不相同，尽管秤常把两者混在一起。
senses.why: physicists needed a word for how much stuff a body contains, and the lump word was the obvious choice.
senses.whyCN: 物理学家需要指称一个物体含有多少实体，那团东西的词自然是首选。

senses.title: The common people
senses.definition: the ordinary people of a society, considered as one body
senses.definitionCN: 社会中的普通人，被当作一个整体来看
senses.example: The reform was popular with the masses but not with the owners.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革受大众欢迎，却不受业主欢迎。
senses.why: crowds pressed together in a square look like one lump, and politics named that lump the masses.
senses.whyCN: 广场上挤在一起的人群看上去就是一团，政治语言把这团叫作「大众」。

senses.title: The religious service
senses.definition: the central service of the Roman Catholic Church, especially one said for the dead
senses.definitionCN: 罗马天主教会的主要礼仪，尤指为亡者举行的那一场
senses.example: They attended early Mass on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 他们星期天参加了清早的弥撒。
senses.why: this sense comes from Latin missa 'dismissal', a different source from massa, and must never be merged with the lump word.
senses.whyCN: 这一义出自拉丁 missa「遣散」，与 massa 不同源，绝不能与「团块」那个词混为一谈。

senses.title: To gather in a crowd
senses.definition: to come together in large numbers, as troops or protesters do
senses.definitionCN: 以大量人数聚拢，如军队或抗议者
senses.example: Troops massed along the border overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 部队一夜之间集结在边境一带。
senses.why: if a mass is many units pressed into one body, then to mass is the act of pressing them together.
senses.whyCN: 既然 mass 是许多单位压成一个整体，那么动词 mass 就是把它们压到一起的动作。

senses.title: Large-scale, for everyone
senses.definition: produced or done on a large scale and aimed at ordinary people
senses.definitionCN: 以大规模制作或进行、面向普通人的
senses.example: Mass production brought the clock within reach of clerks.
senses.exampleCN: 大批量生产让职员也买得起钟表。
senses.why: the adjective turns the lump into a scale word: one lump, then one industry serving a whole market.
senses.whyCN: 形容词把「一团」变成尺度词：先是一团，再是整个服务一方市场的产业。

senses.title: The bulk or greater part
senses.definition: the greater part of something, considered as one undifferentiated body
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的较大部分，被看作一个未加区分的整体
senses.example: The mass of the population lives along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 人口的大部分住在沿海一带。
senses.why: a lump is undivided, so the word also covers the majority when nobody bothers to split it up.
senses.whyCN: 一团是不加分割的，因此当没人去细分时，这个词也指「大多数」。

intro.en: Mass in the sense of a lump comes from Latin massa, generally thought to come from Greek maza 'barley cake'. The church sense comes from Latin missa 'dismissal' and is a separate word.
intro.cn: 「团块」义的 mass 来自拉丁 massa，一般认为源自希腊 maza「大麦饼」；弥撒义来自拉丁 missa「遣散」，是另一个词。

items.en: Maza meant a barley cake or a lump of kneaded dough, and it is generally thought to be the older source behind Latin massa.
items.cn: maza 指大麦饼或揉成团的面，一般认为它是拉丁 massa 更早的来源。

items.en: Massa meant a lump, a mass of metal or dough; the further link to Greek maza is a common view rather than a documented chain.
items.cn: massa 指一团、一块金属或面团；它与希腊 maza 的联系是常见看法，而非有文献可查的链条。

items.en: Missa meant 'dismissal' and became the name of the church service; it has nothing to do with massa and must be kept apart.
items.cn: missa 意为「遣散」，后来成为礼拜仪式的名称；它与 massa 毫无关系，必须分开。

items.en: Both words entered English in the Middle Ages, the lump word through French and the church word through the liturgy.
items.cn: 两个词都在中世纪进入英语：团块义经法语而来，礼仪义经教会用语而来。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the lump word was narrowed by physics to the measurable quantity of matter in a body.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，物理学把「团块」词收窄为物体中可量度的物质的量。

items.en: The first dates for the political and industrial senses are approximate; both words are well attested from the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 政治义与工业义的最早年代为约数；两个词在中世纪都已有充分书证。

note.en: The first group holds forms built on massa plus two near-forms, one of which is famously a different word; the second group holds quantity words.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 massa 的词形，另加一个形近但著名地属于另一个词的词；第二组是表示数量的词。

entries.definition: Built on mass with an adjective suffix, meaning 'huge and solid'; it describes the lump rather than naming it.
entries.definitionCN: 在 mass 上加形容词后缀构成，意为「巨大而结实的」；它描述那团东西而不命名它。

entries.definition: A compact group of mountains, from French massif and the same massa stock; it is a shaped lump of rock.
entries.definitionCN: 指紧凑的一群山，出自法语 massif 与同一 massa 词源；它是被塑造过的一团岩石。

entries.definition: The church service, from Latin missa 'dismissal'; it sounds identical but is not related to the lump word at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指宗教礼仪，出自拉丁 missa「遣散」；读音完全相同，却与「团块」那个词毫无亲缘。

entries.definition: From French amasser, built on masse; to heap things into one lump, usually wealth or evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 出自法语 amasser，由 masse 构成；把东西堆成一团，通常指财富或证据。

entries.definition: The volume or the greater part of something; mass stresses the stuff, bulk stresses the size it takes up.
entries.definitionCN: 指体积或较大部分；mass 强调那团实体，bulk 强调它占的空间。

entries.definition: A pile of separate things stacked up; a mass can be one continuous body, a heap is always many pieces.
entries.definitionCN: 分开的东西堆成一摞；mass 可以是一个连续的整体，heap 永远是许多件。

entries.definition: A large number of people gathered together; the phrase for the masses is a political body, not a crowd in a street.
entries.definitionCN: 聚在一起的一大群人；「大众」是政治意义上的整体，不是街上的一群人。

entries.definition: The force of gravity on a body; mass is how much matter it holds, weight is how hard gravity pulls it.
entries.definitionCN: 重力对物体施加的力；mass 是所含物质的量，weight 是重力拉它的力度。

entries.definition: More than half of a counted group; the bulk phrase means an unsplit body, not a tally.
entries.definitionCN: 被计数群体中过半的部分；而「人口的大部分」是不加细分的整体，不是点数结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin source, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁来源、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin massa was a lump of dough, so mass begins as a shapeless lump.
normal.cn: 拉丁 massa 是一团面，因此 mass 最初就是无定形的一团。

normal.en: The family runs mass, massive, massively, massless and biomass.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 mass、massive、massively、massless 与 biomass。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the scale sense: mass media, mass production, mass market.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出规模义：大众传媒、大批量生产、大众市场。

normal.en: Physics pairs mass with weight, and the two are not interchangeable.
normal.cn: 物理把 mass 与 weight 配对，二者不能互换。

normal.en: Remember that Mass the service comes from Latin missa, not from massa.
normal.cn: 要记住弥撒义的 Mass 出自拉丁 missa，而非 massa。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd in a square pressing into one single dark shape from above.
abstract.cn: 从高处看，广场上的人群挤成一个黑色整体。

abstract.en: Picture a snowball rolling downhill and growing heavier with every turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一个雪球滚下山坡，每转一圈就更沉一些。

abstract.en: Picture a baker's hands pushing a whole table of dough into one lump.
abstract.cn: 想象面包师把整张台面的面按成一团。

examples.en: The nebula contains a mass of gas several times that of the sun.
examples.cn: 这团星云所含气体的质量是太阳的若干倍。

examples.en: Mass tourism has changed the old harbour beyond recognition.
examples.cn: 大众旅游把这个老港口改变得面目全非。

examples.en: Protesters massed outside the hall before the vote.
examples.cn: 表决之前，抗议者在大厅外集结。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马死」——一大群马挤成一团，马死了也堆成一大堆 → 团块、大量

root: 希腊 maza「大麦饼、面团」→ 拉丁 massa「一团、一块」→ 法语 masse → 英语 mass「团块、大量」；物理学再收窄为「质量」；弥撒义的 Mass 另出拉丁 missa「遣散」，与此无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all begin with one lump: dough on a board, a heap of evidence, a measured quantity in physics, a crowd pressed into one body, the bulk of a population, the act of pressing a crowd together, an industry serving everyone, and an unsplit majority.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从一团东西出发：案板上的面团、一堆证据、物理里可量度的量、挤成一个整体的人群、人口的大部分、把人挤到一起的动作、服务所有人的产业，以及不加细分的多数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lump of dough pressed flat across a whole board.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团面被按平，摊满整块案板。

branches.en: THE LUMP AND THE HEAP: one continuous body first, then many pieces pressed into a great quantity.
branches.cn: 一团与一堆：先是连续的一体，再是许多件压成大数量。

branches.en: THE MEASURED LUMP: physics turns the lump into a number that resists acceleration.
branches.cn: 可量度的团：物理学把这团东西变成一个抵抗加速度的数。

branches.en: PEOPLE AS ONE BODY: a crowd pressed together becomes the masses, and an unsplit bulk becomes the majority.
branches.cn: 被当作一体的民众：挤在一起的人群成为大众，未加细分的整体成为多数。

branches.en: THE OTHER WORD: the church service sounds the same but descends from missa, a root of its own.
branches.cn: 另一个词：宗教礼仪读音相同，却出自 missa，自有一个词根。

branches.en: THE ACT AND THE SCALE: pressing things together, and an industry that serves a whole market.
branches.cn: 动作与尺度：把东西压到一起，以及服务整个市场的产业。

intro.en: Mass is a Latin noun of a lump, with a small English family built on it; the church word Mass is a separate stock and is marked as such.
intro.cn: mass 是拉丁语里表示「一团」的名词，英语在其上长出一个不大的词族；弥撒义的 Mass 另有来源，下面单独标出。

latinIntro.en: Latin massa gives mass, massive, massif and amass through French; missa is a different Latin noun and gives only the church sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 massa 经法语给出 mass、massive、massif 与 amass；missa 是另一个拉丁名词，只给出礼仪义。

items.meaning: lump; mass of metal or dough
items.meaningCN: 一团；金属或面团的一块
items.example: The root supplies the picture of a shapeless lump.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「无定形一团」的画面。

items.example: One word covers the lump, the heap and the measured quantity.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词兼指团块、堆与可量度的量。

items.example: A massive wall is one great lump of stone.
items.exampleCN: 一堵厚墙就是一大团石头。

items.example: The massif rises as one block from the plain.
items.exampleCN: 那片山地从平原上整块隆起。

items.example: To amass is to press many things into one heap.
items.exampleCN: amass 就是把许多东西压成一堆。

items.meaning: the total living matter in an area
items.meaningCN: 某一区域内的生物总量
items.example: The prefix narrows the lump to living stuff.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把这团东西限定为活物。

items.example: The compound turns the lump into a sales scale.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把「一团」变成销售的尺度。

items.structure: Latin noun, first declension, separate source
items.example: This root is not related to massa in any way.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根与 massa 没有任何关系。

definition_zh: 重量、分量；重物；负担；重要性、影响力；砝码；权重；在……上加重量
definition_en: how heavy something is, a heavy object, a load on the mind, or the importance given to something
core_image: 一杆老秤的秤砣挂在杆尾，秤杆一点点抬平，货物被吊离地面
scene: 货担一头挂上秤钩，另一头把铁秤砣往外拨，直到秤杆平得纹丝不动。The basket rose once the shopkeeper added one more small weight to the other arm.
sceneCN: 这里 weight 指称出来的分量、物体有多重（第 1 个义项：物体受重力的大小）；句意：店主在另一端又添了一小块秤砣，篮子就升了起来。图中可辨识物件：杆秤、秤砣、秤钩、货担。

pos.zh: 重量；重物；负担；重要性；砝码；权重
在……上加重量；使负重

forms.label: 单数（分量义通常不可数）

senses.title: How heavy a thing is
senses.titleCN: 物体有多重、称出来的分量
senses.definition: the heaviness of a body, measured by the force with which gravity pulls it down
senses.definitionCN: 物体的轻重，由重力向下拉它的力度来衡量
senses.example: The basket rose once the counterweight matched its weight.
senses.exampleCN: 秤砣与货物的分量对上之后，篮子就升了起来。
senses.why: weight comes from Old English gewiht, the noun of wegan 'to carry, to weigh', so it began as the result of weighing.
senses.whyCN: weight 出自古英语 gewiht，是 wegan「搬动、称重」的名词，最初就是「称出来的结果」。

senses.title: A heavy object used as a load
senses.titleCN: 作为配重或压载的重物
senses.definition: a solid object heavy enough to hold something down or to serve as a counterbalance
senses.definitionCN: 重到足以压住某物或充当平衡物的实体物件
senses.example: The diver wore lead weights on his belt.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员腰带上挂着铅制配重。
senses.why: once the noun meant a measured amount, it could also name the metal piece that provides that amount.
senses.whyCN: 名词既能指称出的量，也就能指提供这个量的那块金属。

senses.title: A burden on the mind
senses.definition: a worry or responsibility that presses on someone like a heavy load
senses.definitionCN: 像重物一样压在某人身上的忧虑或责任
senses.example: The weight of debt kept him awake at night.
senses.exampleCN: 债务的重压让他夜里睡不着。
senses.why: the physical pull downward is felt in the body, and English extended that sensation to care and responsibility.
senses.whyCN: 向下的物理拉力在身体上有感觉，英语把这种感受延伸到忧虑与责任。

senses.title: Power to influence
senses.definition: the influence or authority that a person, opinion or argument has
senses.definitionCN: 某个人、某种意见或论证所具有的影响力与权威
senses.example: Her opinion carries great weight on the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 在委员会里，她的意见很有分量。
senses.why: a heavy thing is hard to move, so an opinion with weight is one that others cannot easily brush aside.
senses.whyCN: 重的东西推不动，因此有分量的意见别人不容易轻轻拨开。

senses.title: A standard piece for scales
senses.definition: a piece of metal of known mass used with a balance to measure other loads
senses.definitionCN: 质量已知的金属块，配天平用来量别的货物
senses.example: The brass weights sat in a velvet-lined box.
senses.exampleCN: 铜砝码装在一只衬绒的盒子里。
senses.why: the sense narrowed to the object that embodies a fixed amount, which is how a market keeps its measures honest.
senses.whyCN: 这一义收窄到「固定分量的载体」，集市靠它保证称量公道。

senses.title: Share in a total
senses.titleCN: 在总分中占的权重比例
senses.definition: the relative importance assigned to one item within a total, as in grading or statistics
senses.definitionCN: 某一项在总体中所占的相对重要性，如评分或统计中的比例
senses.example: Each question carries a different weight in the final score.
senses.exampleCN: 每道题在总分里占的权重不同。
senses.why: if influence is weight, then a share of influence can be counted as a weight in a formula.
senses.whyCN: 既然影响力即分量，那么一份影响力就可以在公式里记成一个权重。

senses.title: To hold something down
senses.definition: to add a heavy object to something so that it stays in place or sinks
senses.definitionCN: 给某物加上重物，使其留在原处或下沉
senses.example: They weighted the net so it would sink straight down.
senses.exampleCN: 他们给网加了重物，好让它直直沉下去。
senses.why: the verb is the action behind the noun: to give a thing the heaviness that a weight provides.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词背后的动作：把砝码能提供的那种分量加给某物。

senses.title: The preponderance of evidence
senses.titleCN: 证据整体的压倒性分量
senses.definition: the collective force of evidence when it is weighed as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把证据作为一个整体来称量时形成的合力
senses.example: The weight of evidence favoured the defence.
senses.exampleCN: 证据的分量偏向辩方。
senses.why: a set of facts is put on the scales together, and whichever pan sinks carries the weight.
senses.whyCN: 一组事实被一起放上天平，沉下去的那一端就带着分量。

intro.en: Weight is Old English gewiht, the noun of wegan 'to carry, to move, to weigh'. It belongs to the Germanic family and has no Latin counterpart.
intro.cn: weight 是古英语 gewiht，即 wegan「搬动、称重」的名词。它属日耳曼语族，在拉丁语里没有对应同族词。

items.en: Wegan meant 'to carry, to move something from place to place' and also 'to weigh', since lifting a thing is how you judge its heft.
items.cn: wegan 意为「搬动、把东西挪位」，也指「称重」，因为把东西提起来正是判断其轻重的办法。

items.en: Gewiht was the noun of that verb, naming the amount a thing weighs; the ge- prefix was later dropped.
items.cn: gewiht 是那个动词的名词，指某物所具的分量；前缀后来脱落。

items.en: Middle English weight kept the everyday sense of heaviness and added the sense of a standard piece used on a balance.
items.cn: 中古英语 weight 保留了「轻重」的日常义，并加上「天平上用标准块」的意思。

items.en: In markets the word became a guarantee of honest measure, which is why weights and measures are named together.
items.cn: 在集市上，这个词成了公道称量的保证，因此「砝码与度量」总是并称。

items.en: The senses of burden, influence and statistical share all grow from the same downward pull felt in the body.
items.cn: 负担、影响力与统计权重诸义，都从身体感受到的那股向下拉力长出来。

items.en: The first dates for the figurative and statistical senses are approximate; the core noun is recorded from the Old English period.
items.cn: 比喻义与统计义的最早年代为约数；核心名词义在古英语时期已有记录。

note.en: The first group holds Germanic relatives and one homophone from an unrelated root; the second group holds words that overlap with weight.
note.cn: 第一组是日耳曼同族词，另加一个来自无关词根的同音词；第二组是与 weight 部分同义的词。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun, from Old English wegan 'to carry, to weigh'; weight is its derived noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词，出自古英语 wegan「搬动、称重」；weight 是它的派生名词。

entries.definition: Built on weight with -y, meaning 'heavy or serious'; it is a derived adjective, not another root.
entries.definitionCN: 在 weight 上加 -y 构成，意为「沉重的、有分量的」；它是派生形容词，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: The past participle used as an adjective, meaning 'loaded down' or 'adjusted by a factor'.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词作形容词，意为「加了重的」或「按系数调整过的」。

entries.definition: A homophone from Old North French waitier, of Germanic watch stock; it means to stay expecting, not to carry heft.
entries.definitionCN: 同音词，出自古北法语 waitier，属日耳曼「守望」一系；意为等候，与承载分量无关。

entries.definition: The quantity of matter in a body; weight is the gravitational pull on that matter, so the two differ in physics.
entries.definitionCN: 物体所含物质的量；weight 是重力对这团物质的拉力，因此物理上二者不同。

entries.definition: A load carried or endured; it stresses having to bear something, while weight stresses the pressing down.
entries.definitionCN: 需要背负或承受的负荷；burden 强调必须承担，weight 强调向下压。

entries.definition: The goods or mass carried by a person or vehicle; it is countable in a way weight usually is not.
entries.definitionCN: 人或车辆所载的货物；它可数，而 weight 通常不可数。

entries.definition: The quality of mattering; weight conveys the same idea through a physical picture of pressing down.
entries.definitionCN: 「要紧」这一性质；weight 通过向下压的物理画面传达同样的意思。

entries.definition: The attractive force between bodies; weight is what that force amounts to for a particular object.
entries.definitionCN: 物体之间的吸引力；weight 是这股力对某个具体物体所成的结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Old English root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的古英语词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Old English wegan 'to carry, to weigh' gives the noun gewiht, which became weight.
normal.cn: 古英语 wegan「搬动、称重」给出名词 gewiht，后来变成 weight。

normal.en: The family runs weight, weigh, weighty, weightless and overweight.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 weight、weigh、weighty、weightless 与 overweight。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the everyday sense: lose weight, gain weight, body weight.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出日常义：减重、增重、体重。

normal.en: The phrase for having influence, carry weight, is built on the same downward pull.
normal.cn: 表示「有影响力」的那个固定说法，仍建立在那股向下的拉力上。

normal.en: Physics keeps mass and weight apart: mass is the amount, weight is the pull.
normal.cn: 物理把质量与重量分开：质量是含量，重量是拉力。

abstract.en: Picture a scale beam slowly levelling while the basket lifts clear of the ground.
abstract.cn: 想象秤杆慢慢抬平，篮子离开地面的那一刻。

abstract.en: Picture a shoulder bending a little lower under a strap nobody else can see.
abstract.cn: 想象一边肩膀微微低下去，而肩上那根带子别人看不见。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of papers on one side of a balance, sinking it without a sound.
abstract.cn: 想象天平一端堆着一叠纸，不出声地把它压沉。

examples.en: The doctor tracked the patient's weight over six months.
examples.cn: 医生在半年里跟踪病人的体重。

examples.en: In the regression model each predictor is given a different weight.
examples.cn: 在回归模型中，每个预测变量被赋予不同的权重。

examples.en: The weight of evidence now points to a much older settlement.
examples.cn: 如今证据的分量指向一处年代更早得多的聚落。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂特」——喂得特别多，人就增重 → 重量、分量

root: 古英语 wegan「搬动、称重」→ 名词 gewiht「所称出的分量」→ 中古英语 weight；属日耳曼语族，拉丁语中无同族词，「负担、影响力、权重」义由向下的拉力引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all hang from one downward pull: the heaviness on a scale, the metal piece that matches it, the load on the mind, the influence that cannot be brushed aside, the standard brass block, a share in a total, the act of pressing something down, and the combined pull of all the evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都挂在同一股向下的拉力上：秤上的轻重、与之相配的金属块、心上的负荷、拨不开的影响力、标准铜块、总分里的一份、把东西压下去的动作，以及全部证据合成的分量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a counterweight slid along a beam until the beam levels.
core.cn: 核心意象：秤砣沿秤杆滑动，直到秤杆抬平。

branches.en: THE MEASURE AND ITS EMBODIMENT: how heavy a thing is, and the brass block that stands for a fixed amount of it.
branches.cn: 度量与其载体：物体有多重，以及代表固定分量的那块铜。

branches.en: THE LOAD AND THE ACT: a heavy object that holds things down, and the deed of adding it.
branches.cn: 重物与动作：压住东西的重物，以及把重物加上去的动作。

branches.en: THE MIND UNDER LOAD: worry and debt press the body exactly as a strap does.
branches.cn: 承重的心：忧虑与债务对身体的作用，正如一根背带。

branches.en: INFLUENCE MADE COUNTABLE: an opinion that cannot be brushed aside, and a share of it written into a formula.
branches.cn: 可计数的影响力：拨不开的意见，以及写进公式的那一份。

branches.en: EVIDENCE ON THE SCALES: all the facts placed in one pan, and whichever side sinks carries the weight.
branches.cn: 放上天平的证据：全部事实放进一端，沉下哪边，分量就在哪边。

intro.en: Weight is a Germanic word, so instead of Latin parts the entry breaks it into an Old English verb, its noun, and the English suffixes grown on it.
intro.cn: weight 是日耳曼语词，因此本条不拆拉丁成分，而拆解古英语动词、它的名词，以及在其上长出的英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin relative for weight; wegan and gewiht belong to the Germanic stock, and the Latin-looking forms in this family are borrowed or separately formed.
latinIntro.cn: weight 在拉丁语中没有同族词；wegan 与 gewiht 属日耳曼语一系，这个词族里看似拉丁形的成员都是借词或另行构成。

items.meaning: to carry; to move; to weigh
items.example: Lifting a thing is how its heft is judged.
items.exampleCN: 把东西提起来，就是判断其轻重的办法。

items.structure: Old English noun of wegan, with ge-
items.example: The prefix later dropped away, leaving weight.
items.exampleCN: 前缀后来脱落，留下 weight。

items.example: One noun covers the measure and the meaning.
items.exampleCN: 一个名词同时覆盖度量与意义。

items.example: To weigh an argument is to put it on the scales.
items.exampleCN: 权衡一个论点，就是把它放上天平。

items.example: A weighty matter is one that presses hard.
items.exampleCN: 沉重的事情就是压得很紧的事。

items.example: The suffix removes the downward pull entirely.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把向下的拉力整个去掉。

items.example: The noun names the act of giving each item its share.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指给每一项分配份额的动作。

items.example: The prefix says the pull exceeds the proper amount.
items.exampleCN: 前缀说明分量超出了应有的限度。

items.example: The opposite prefix says the pull falls short.
items.exampleCN: 相反的前缀说明分量不足。

definition_zh: 体积；容积；容量；音量；卷；册；总量；交易量；流量
definition_en: the amount of space that something fills or can hold, or a book bound as one of a set, or the loudness of a sound
core_image: 一张写满字的羊皮纸被卷成筒，旁边立着一只装到刻度的玻璃量筒
scene: 演出开始前，剧场里的交头接耳越来越响，调音台前的人伸手拧动旋钮。She turned the knob until the volume of the hall speakers dropped to a whisper.
sceneCN: 这里 volume 指声音的强弱（第 5 个义项：音量，即可由设备旋钮调节的响度）；句意：她把旋钮拧到大厅音箱只剩耳语般的声响。图中可辨识物件：调音台旋钮、音箱、刻度盘、贴着标签的线缆。

pos.zh: 体积；容积；容量；音量；卷；册；总量

forms.label: 单数（不可数，指体积、容量、音量）
复数（指多册书或多股流量）
形容词（体积的；按体积计的）
形容词（卷帙浩繁的；宽大的）

derivatives.zh: 卷帙浩繁的；（衣物）宽大的

senses.title: A book as a physical object
senses.definition: a book, especially a large or scholarly one, considered as a physical object
senses.definitionCN: 一本书，尤指厚重或学术性的书，作为实体来看待
senses.example: A single volume of the atlas weighed as much as a sack of grain.
senses.exampleCN: 那套地图集的一册就重得像一袋谷子。
senses.why: Latin volumen first meant a roll of papyrus, and the name stayed with the bound object when rolls became folded books.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 volumen 最初指一卷纸草，卷轴改成折叠装订的书以后，这个名字仍留在装订好的实体上。

senses.title: One book within a set
senses.titleCN: 成套书或丛书中的一卷
senses.definition: one of several books that together make up a single work or series
senses.definitionCN: 若干部书合起来构成一部作品或一套丛书，其中的一部
senses.example: The encyclopedia runs to twelve volumes.
senses.exampleCN: 这套百科全书共有十二卷。
senses.why: A large work was once rolled out one scroll at a time, so each separate book kept the name that belonged to the whole.
senses.whyCN: 大部头著作原是一卷一卷展开的，因此每一册都沿用了属于整部书的名称。

senses.title: The space a body fills
senses.definition: the amount of three-dimensional space occupied by a substance or object
senses.definitionCN: 物质或物体所占据的三维空间的大小
senses.example: The volume of the block was found by multiplying its three sides.
senses.exampleCN: 这块方料的体积由三条边长相乘求得。
senses.why: A rolled bundle takes up room, so the amount of room it displaces became a measurable sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 卷起来的一团东西占地方，它排开的空间有多大，就成了这个词可测量的一义。

senses.title: The room inside a container
senses.definition: the amount of space inside a container, measured in litres or cubic units
senses.definitionCN: 容器内部可容纳的空间，以升或立方单位计量
senses.example: The tank's volume is just under forty litres.
senses.exampleCN: 这个罐子的容积略小于四十升。
senses.why: Inside and outside are the same measurement seen from two sides, so the word covers what a thing fills and what it can hold.
senses.whyCN: 里面与外面是同一测量从两侧看，因此这个词既指物体占去的空间，也指容器装得下的空间。

senses.title: Loudness of sound
senses.definition: the strength or loudness of a sound, especially as controlled on a device
senses.definitionCN: 声音的强度或响度，尤指可由设备调节的那种
senses.example: He kept the volume low so the lecture would not wake the neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 他把音量调得很低，免得讲座吵醒邻居。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century acoustics needed a word for how much sound a source sends out, and it borrowed the idea of bulk: more sound fills more space.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的声学需要一个词表示声源送出多少声音，于是借用了「体积」的思路：声音越多，占的空间越大。

senses.title: A large total quantity
senses.definition: a large quantity of something considered as a whole, such as work, applications or sales
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物当作整体来看时的大量总额，如工作量、申请量或销售量
senses.example: The volume of applications doubled after the scholarship was announced.
senses.exampleCN: 奖学金消息公布后，申请量翻了一倍。
senses.why: Bulk came to mean sheer quantity, not only physical size, so any large total could be called a volume.
senses.whyCN: 「大块」逐渐指纯粹的数量，而不只是物理大小，于是任何大总额都能叫 volume。

senses.title: Trade over a period
senses.definition: the total amount of goods, shares or money traded in a market over a period
senses.definitionCN: 市场上在一定时期内成交的商品、股票或金额的总量
senses.example: Share prices fell even as trading volume rose.
senses.exampleCN: 股价下跌，成交量却在上升。
senses.why: Markets count bulk in numbers, so the word moved from physical size to the size of a flow of trades.
senses.whyCN: 市场用数字来计「大块」，这个词便从物理大小转指交易这股流的大小。

senses.title: Traffic or data flow
senses.definition: the amount of traffic, calls or data passing through a network or route in a period
senses.definitionCN: 一定时期内经过网络或线路的交通、通话或数据的总量
senses.example: The city's data volume triples during the evening.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的数据流量在晚间增至三倍。
senses.why: A flow is measured like a substance: how much passes a point in a given time, which is bulk applied to movement.
senses.whyCN: 流量像物质一样被计量：一定时间内有多少经过某一点，这就是把「体积」用在运动上。

intro.en: Volume comes through Old French from Latin volumen, a thing rolled, especially a roll of writing, built on volvere 'to roll'. The book sense is oldest; the senses of bulk, capacity and loudness are later extensions.
intro.cn: volume 经古法语来自拉丁 volumen「卷起之物、书卷、卷轴」，由 volvere「滚动、卷」构成。书卷义最古老，体积、容量与音量诸义都是后来的引申。

items.en: Volvere meant to roll, to turn round, to unwind; the image is a hand rolling a sheet of papyrus into a cylinder.
items.cn: volvere 意为「滚动、转动、展开」，画面是一只手把一张纸草卷成圆筒。

items.en: Volumen, from the same verb, named a thing rolled up: a coil, a whirl, and above all a roll of writing.
items.cn: volumen 由同一动词构成，指卷起来的东西：一卷、一团旋涡，最常用的是书写用的卷轴。

items.en: Old French volume carried the word into English in the fourteenth century, still with the sense of a book or a roll.
items.cn: 古法语 volume 在十四世纪把这个词带入英语，仍带「书卷、卷轴」的意思。

items.en: The sense of bulk or mass is recorded from the sixteenth century, when the space a rolled thing fills was treated as measurable.
items.cn: 「体积、大块」义自十六世纪有记录，当时把卷起之物所占的空间当作可测量之物。

items.en: The acoustic sense of loudness is a nineteenth-century extension, when instruments began to control how much sound filled a room.
items.cn: 声音响度这一声学义是十九世纪的引申，当时设备开始控制有多少声音充满一个房间。

items.en: The first recorded dates for the bulk and sound senses are approximate; the book sense is well attested from the medieval period.
items.cn: 体积义与音量义的最早记录年代为约数；书卷义在中世纪已有充分记录。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin root of rolling and is easily confused; the second group offers near meanings for size, room and loudness.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「滚动」词根，容易混淆；第二组给出「大小、容量、响度」的近义说法。

entries.definition: An adjective from the same Latin noun, meaning bulky or filling many pages; it describes the bulk, not the book.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一拉丁名词构成的形容词，指庞大或篇幅浩繁；它描述的是体量，不是书本身。

entries.definition: A scroll-shaped ornament in architecture, from Latin voluta, itself from volvere 'to roll'; the link is the curl, not the book.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑上的涡卷形装饰，来自拉丁 voluta，而 voluta 又出自 volvere「卷」；联系在卷曲的形状，不在书。

entries.definition: From Latin volubilis 'turning easily', built on volvere; it describes fluent, fast-turning speech, not size.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 volubilis「易于转动」，由 volvere 构成；形容说话流利、滔滔不绝，与大小无关。

entries.definition: From con- 'together' plus volvere: rolled together, hence coiled or intricate; it is about tangled shape or argument.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-「一起」加 volvere 构成：卷在一起，因此指盘绕或繁复；说的是缠绕的形状或论证。

entries.definition: From Latin voluntas 'will', not from volvere; it means done by choice and has nothing to do with rolling or books.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 voluntas「意愿」，而非 volvere；意为出于自愿，与滚动或书卷无关。

entries.definition: The space a container can hold; it answers how much fits, while volume can also name the bulk outside.
entries.definitionCN: 容器装得下的空间；回答能装多少，而 volume 也能指物体外在的体量。

entries.definition: The sheer mass or size of a body, without the measured precision that volume carries.
entries.definitionCN: 物体的庞大体量与体积，不带 volume 那种精确测量的意味。

entries.definition: The perceived strength of a sound; volume is the everyday name for the setting that controls it.
entries.definitionCN: 人耳感到的声音强度；volume 是控制这一强度的日常说法。

entries.definition: A countable or measurable amount; volume stresses the whole bulk rather than the count.
entries.definitionCN: 可数或可测的数量；volume 强调整体的量，而非逐个计数。

entries.definition: A large scholarly book; it is a near synonym of one sense of volume but more informal in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 厚重的大部头学术书；与 volume 的某一义相近，但语气更随意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Volvere is Latin for to roll: a volumen was a roll of papyrus before it was ever a book.
normal.cn: volvere 是拉丁语「卷、滚」：volumen 先是纸草卷轴，后来才成为书。

normal.en: The family runs volume, volumes, volumetric, voluminous, volumetry.
normal.cn: 同族词有 volume、volumes、volumetric、voluminous、volumetry。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the everyday senses: sales volume, volume control, volume of traffic.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出日常义：销售量、音量控制、交通流量。

normal.en: Physics measures volume in cubic metres and capacity in litres, one measurement seen from two sides.
normal.cn: 物理用立方米量体积、用升量容积，是同一测量从两侧看。

normal.en: The sound sense came with acoustics: a knob on a speaker changes how much sound fills the room.
normal.cn: 音量义随声学而来：音箱上的旋钮改变有多少声音充满房间。

abstract.en: Picture a scroll rolling itself shut, then standing on a shelf as a thick book.
abstract.cn: 想象一卷纸自己卷合起来，然后立在书架上变成一本厚书。

abstract.en: Picture a glass tank whose water line climbs as stones are dropped in.
abstract.cn: 想象一只玻璃槽，石头丢进去，水面一格一格往上升。

abstract.en: Picture a dial turning down and a whole hall going quiet.
abstract.cn: 想象一个旋钮被拧小，整个大厅随之安静下来。

examples.en: The report fills three volumes and still ends before the war.
examples.cn: 这份报告写满了三卷，却仍写到战争之前就停住了。

examples.en: Measure the volume of the stone by the water it displaces.
examples.cn: 用石头排开的水量来测它的体积。

examples.en: He lowered the volume when the baby fell asleep.
examples.cn: 孩子睡着后，他把音量调低了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「vo（我）+ lu（路）+ me（么）」——我一路走过去，书一卷卷变厚，声音也一格一格调低

root: 拉丁 volvere「滚动、卷」→ 拉丁 volumen「卷起之物、书卷、卷轴」→ 古法语 volume → 英语 volume；体积义由「卷成的一团」引申，音量义为近代声学用法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses leave one rolled sheet: it becomes a bound book, then one book of a set, then the space a body fills, the room a vessel holds, the bulk of sound, the bulk of a quantity, the bulk of trade, and the bulk of a flow.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一张卷起的纸出发：它先成为装订的书，再成为成套书中的一册，然后是物体占的空间、容器装得下的空间、声音的量、某事物的总量、交易量，最后是流经某处的流量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a written sheet rolled into a scroll, which becomes a book and then any measured bulk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写字的纸卷成卷轴，随后成为书，再成为任何可量的体量。

branches.en: THE BOOK: the roll becomes a bound book, and a set of them is counted in volumes.
branches.cn: 书卷：卷轴变成装订的书，成套的书则以卷来计数。

branches.en: BULK OUTSIDE AND AMOUNT: the space a body fills grows into any large total.
branches.cn: 外在体量与总量：物体占的空间扩大为任何大总额。

branches.en: ROOM INSIDE: a container's capacity is the same measurement turned inward.
branches.cn: 内部空间：容器的容积是同一测量转向内侧。

branches.en: SOUND: acoustics borrowed bulk for how much sound a source sends out.
branches.cn: 声音：声学借「体量」来指声源送出多少声音。

branches.en: FLOW: trade and traffic are measured as bulk passing a point.
branches.cn: 流动：交易与交通被当作经过某一点的体量来计量。

intro.en: Volume is a Latin noun of rolling, and the same root builds several English adjectives and technical terms.
intro.cn: volume 是一个表示「卷」的拉丁名词，同一词根还构成若干英语形容词与技术术语。

latinIntro.en: Latin volvere 'to roll' gives volumen and, through it, volume; the root also gives volute, voluble and convoluted.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 volvere「卷、滚」衍生 volumen，再衍生 volume；这个词根还衍生 volute、voluble 与 convoluted。

items.example: The root describes the hand that rolls a sheet shut.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根描述把纸卷合起来的那只手。

items.meaning: a thing rolled; a scroll; a book
items.example: A volumen was a scroll before it was ever a book.
items.exampleCN: volumen 先是卷轴，后来才指书。

items.example: One volume of the set was missing from the shelf.
items.exampleCN: 书架上那套书少了一册。

items.example: The index fills two volumes.
items.exampleCN: 索引占了两卷。

items.example: The lab reports concentration in volumetric terms.
items.exampleCN: 实验室按体积给出浓度。

items.example: Her notes ran to voluminous files.
items.exampleCN: 她的笔记积成了浩繁的卷宗。

items.example: The mixture is measured volumetrically, not by weight.
items.exampleCN: 这混合物按体积量取，而不按重量。

items.example: Volumetry gives the size of the sample without weighing it.
items.exampleCN: 体积测定法不用称重就能给出样品的大小。

items.structure: Greek suffix through Latin and French
items.meaning: the act or science of measuring
items.example: The ending turns a measuring act into a name, as in geometry.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把测量动作变成一个名称，如几何学一词。

definition_zh: 力；力量；力气；武力；强制；效力；部队；人力；迫使
definition_en: physical strength or power, or the power that makes something happen or makes someone act against resistance
core_image: 一根被重物压弯的钢梁架在千斤顶上，梁身一点点被顶回直线
scene: 工地上一根钢梁被落下的重物压弯，工人架起千斤顶，梁身一点点回直。The jack applied a steady force until the bent beam straightened.
sceneCN: 这里 force 指使物体形状或运动改变的机械推力（第 1 个义项：物理意义上的力）；句意：千斤顶持续施加力，直到弯梁被顶直。图中可辨识物件：千斤顶、弯钢梁、落下的配重、地上的安全帽。

pos.zh: 力；力量；武力；效力；部队；人力
迫使；强行推动；勉强打开

senses.title: A push or pull that changes motion
senses.titleCN: 改变运动或形状的推拉力
senses.definition: a physical push or pull that can change the speed, direction or shape of a body
senses.definitionCN: 能改变物体速度、方向或形状的物理推拉作用
senses.example: The net force on the cart equals its mass times its acceleration.
senses.exampleCN: 小车所受的合力等于质量乘以加速度。
senses.why: Latin fortis meant strong, and mechanics took the word for the measurable quantity that makes a body move or bend.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 fortis 意为强壮，力学借这个词来指使物体运动或弯曲的可测之量。

senses.title: Strength of body or blow
senses.definition: muscular strength, or the power carried by a blow, a throw or a wave
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉的力量，或一击、一掷、一道浪所带的威力
senses.example: The force of the wave knocked the swimmer off her feet.
senses.exampleCN: 浪的力量把游泳者掀翻。
senses.why: Before physics existed, force was simply the strength that a body or a blow carries.
senses.whyCN: 在物理学出现之前，force 就是身体或一击所带的力气。

senses.title: Compulsion against resistance
senses.titleCN: 对抵抗施加的强制与武力
senses.definition: the use of pressure or violence to make someone do something against their will
senses.definitionCN: 用压力或暴力使人违背意愿地做某事
senses.example: The door yielded only to force.
senses.exampleCN: 那扇门只有靠强力才被打开。
senses.why: A strong hand can push a person as it pushes a door, so bodily strength became compulsion.
senses.whyCN: 强壮的手能推人，也能推门，于是体力这一义引申为强制。

senses.title: Binding power of law or rule
senses.definition: the legal or formal power that makes a rule, agreement or order binding
senses.definitionCN: 使规则、协议或命令具有约束力的法律或正式效力
senses.example: The new rules came into force at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定在午夜开始生效。
senses.why: A rule in force has the strength of an authority behind it, as if it could push a person into line.
senses.whyCN: 处于生效状态的规则背后有权威的力量，仿佛能把人推回队列。

senses.title: Power to convince
senses.definition: the strength of an argument, feeling or habit to move people's minds or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 论点、情感或习惯打动人心、改变行为的力量
senses.example: The force of her argument silenced the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她论证的力量让全场静了下来。
senses.why: An argument moves a mind the way a hand moves a body, so the same word covers mental pushing.
senses.whyCN: 论证推动人心，正如手推动身体，因此同一个词也指精神上的推力。

senses.title: An armed body of people
senses.definition: an organized body of soldiers, police or other armed personnel
senses.definitionCN: 有组织的军人、警察或其他武装人员群体
senses.example: The peacekeeping force reached the border at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 维和部队在黎明时抵达边境。
senses.why: Strength collected into a unit is spoken of as a force, a collective use of the same noun.
senses.whyCN: 把力量聚成一个单位，就说成一支 force，这是同一名词的集体用法。

senses.title: Manpower counted as a group
senses.definition: the number of people available for work, or a group treated as a single power
senses.definitionCN: 可供工作的人数，或被当作一股力量的人群
senses.example: The factory's labour force grew by a third in two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂的劳动力两年间增加了三分之一。
senses.why: Once force meant strength in numbers, any body of workers could be counted as a force.
senses.whyCN: 当 force 指人数所聚的力量，任何一群工人也能被计为一股 force。

senses.title: To make something happen by pressure
senses.definition: to cause something to happen or to move by using pressure, effort or necessity
senses.definitionCN: 借助压力、努力或情势使某事发生或移动
senses.example: Illness forced him to give up the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 疾病迫使他放弃夜班。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb: to put strength behind something until it yields.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：把力量压到某事背后，直到它让步。

intro.en: Force comes through Old French from late Latin fortia, a plural noun of strength built on fortis 'strong'. The physics sense dates from the seventeenth century, while the military sense is a collective use of the same noun.
intro.cn: force 经古法语来自晚期拉丁 fortia，这是由 fortis「强壮」构成的表「力量」的复数名词。物理义始于十七世纪，军事义则是同一名词的集体用法。

items.en: Fortis meant strong, mighty, able to resist; it described bodies, walls and men alike.
items.cn: fortis 意为强壮、有力量、能抵抗；它既能形容身体，也能形容城墙与人。

items.en: Late Latin fortia, a plural noun built on fortis, named strength or might; it is the form generally cited behind the French word.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 fortia 是由 fortis 构成的复数名词，指力量、威力；一般认为法语词就出自这个形式。

items.en: Old French force carried the noun into English in the thirteenth century with the senses of strength, violence and legal power.
items.cn: 古法语 force 在十三世纪把这个名词带入英语，带有力量、暴力与法律效力诸义。

items.en: By the medieval period force already covered armed bodies and the binding power of law, two branches that still run side by side.
items.cn: 到中世纪，force 已兼指武装队伍与法律的约束力，这两条分支至今并行。

items.en: Mechanics gave force its precise sense of a measurable push or pull, a use that became standard in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 力学赋予 force 可测量的推拉作用这一精确含义，这一用法在十七世纪成为标准。

items.en: The first dates for the physics sense and for the collective military sense are approximate; the noun itself is well attested from the medieval period.
items.cn: 物理义与集体军事义的最早记录年代为约数；这个名词本身在中世纪已有充分记录。

note.en: The first group either shares the Latin adjective for strong or merely looks like force; the second group separates force from neighbouring words for power and pressure.
note.cn: 第一组或共享那个表示「强壮」的拉丁形容词，或只是形似 force；第二组把 force 与相邻的「权力、压力」等词区分开。

entries.definition: From Latin fortis through French, but it names a stronghold, a place built to resist, not strength itself.
entries.definitionCN: 经法语来自拉丁 fortis，但指堡垒，即一座为抵抗而建的处所，不是力量本身。

entries.definition: From Italian forte 'strong', ultimately Latin fortis; it names a person's strong point, or a loud passage in music.
entries.definitionCN: 来自意大利语 forte「强壮」，最终出自拉丁 fortis；指一个人的长处，或音乐中响亮的段落。

entries.definition: A strengthened place, built on the same Latin adjective; it is a noun of place, not of power.
entries.definitionCN: 加固的城堡，由同一拉丁形容词构成；是表示地点的名词，不是力量。

entries.definition: From in- plus force: to put strength behind a rule so that it is obeyed.
entries.definitionCN: 由表「进入」的前缀加 force 构成：把力量放到规则背后，使其被遵守。

entries.definition: A smithy and the verb to shape metal; it comes from Latin fabrica 'workshop', not from fortis, so it only looks related.
entries.definitionCN: 指铁匠铺与锻打金属的动词；来自拉丁 fabrica「作坊」，而非 fortis，只是形似而已。

entries.definition: The quality of being strong in body or material; force can also mean the push itself.
entries.definitionCN: 身体或材料强健的性质；force 还能指推拉作用本身。

entries.definition: A broader word for ability or authority; force adds the idea of pressure applied.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指能力或权威的更宽说法；force 多一层「施加压力」的意思。

entries.definition: A steady push spread over a surface; force is the total push, pressure is that push divided by area.
entries.definitionCN: 分布在表面上的持续推力；force 是总推力，pressure 是单位面积上的推力。

entries.definition: Force used to injure or damage; it is the destructive edge of force.
entries.definitionCN: 用以伤害或破坏的力量；是 force 中带破坏性的那一面。

entries.definition: A verb for making someone act; force can do the same but also names the strength behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 使人行动的一个动词；force 也能这样用，但同时指背后的力量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Fortis is Latin for strong, and fortitude is the strength to endure.
normal.cn: fortis 是拉丁语「强壮」，fortitude 就是能坚持的力量。

normal.en: The family runs force, forced, forceful, enforce and reinforce.
normal.cn: 同族词有 force、forced、forceful、enforce 与 reinforce。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the main senses: come into force, labour force, air force, by force.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出主要义项：生效、劳动力、空军、强行地。

normal.en: Physics measures force in newtons, and every force has a direction.
normal.cn: 物理以牛顿为单位量力，每一个力都有方向。

normal.en: Law says a rule in force is one that can be enforced.
normal.cn: 法律说一条正在生效的规则，就是能被强制执行的那条。

abstract.en: Picture a bent beam slowly returning to a straight line under a jack.
abstract.cn: 想象一根弯梁在千斤顶下慢慢回到直线。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd leaning together against a gate until the hinges give way.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人一起压在门上，直到铰链撑不住。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing a stamp down hard enough to leave a mark.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手用力压下印章，留下清晰的痕迹。

examples.en: The engineers calculated the force needed to lift the span.
examples.cn: 工程师算出了抬起这跨梁所需的力。

examples.en: The old law is no longer in force.
examples.cn: 那条旧法律已不再生效。

examples.en: A strong wind forced the ferry to stay in port.
examples.cn: 大风迫使渡轮留在港内。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「for（为了）+ ce（策）」——为了推行一套策，就得使出力气；force 力量、武力、迫使

root: 拉丁 fortis「强壮」→ 晚期拉丁 fortia「力量」（复数）→ 古法语 force「力量、武力」→ 英语 force；物理「力」义自十七世纪力学，「部队」义由「兵力」的集体用法而来。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from one strong hand: the hand pushes a body, shows its own strength, compels a person, backs a rule, moves a mind, gathers into a troop, is counted as manpower, and finally acts as a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一只强壮的手长出：手推动物体、显出力气、强迫人、为规则撑腰、推动人心、聚成队伍、被计为人力，最后转为动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a strong hand that pushes until something yields.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只强壮的手一直推，直到某物让步。

branches.en: PUSH AND STRENGTH: a measurable push, and the plain strength a body or blow carries.
branches.cn: 推力与力气：可测量的推拉作用，以及身体或一击所带的直白力量。

branches.en: COMPULSION: the same push turned against a resisting person.
branches.cn: 强制：同一个推力转向一个抵抗的人。

branches.en: POWER BEHIND WORDS: a rule is enforced, an argument convinces, both by invisible pushing.
