branches.cn: 言语背后的力量：规则被强制执行，论证说服人心，都是看不见的推力。

branches.en: STRENGTH IN NUMBERS: armed men and workers are gathered and counted as one force.
branches.cn: 人多成势：武装人员与工人被聚拢，计作一股力量。

branches.en: THE VERB: the hand that pushed becomes the act of forcing.
branches.cn: 动词：曾经推动的那只手，变成「迫使」这个动作。

intro.en: Force is a Latin noun of strength that became an English noun, verb and a whole family of derived words.
intro.cn: force 是一个表示力量的拉丁名词，在英语里成为名词、动词，并衍生出整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin fortis 'strong' gives fortia and force, and also fortitude, fort and fortress; the English prefix en- builds enforce from the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fortis「强壮」衍生 fortia 与 force，也衍生 fortitude、fort 与 fortress；英语前缀 en- 由同一词干构成 enforce。

items.example: The adjective supplies the strength behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词为整个词族提供「力量」的底子。

items.structure: late Latin plural noun from fortis
items.example: The late Latin plural is the form usually cited behind the French noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个晚期拉丁复数，一般认为就是法语名词背后的形式。

items.example: The jack applied a steady force.
items.exampleCN: 千斤顶持续施加力。

items.structure: force plus plural or third-person ending
items.example: Enemy forces withdrew from the valley.
items.exampleCN: 敌军撤出了山谷。

items.example: She gave a forced smile and left.
items.exampleCN: 她勉强笑了一下就走开了。

items.example: The chair gave a forceful reply.
items.exampleCN: 主席作了有力的答复。

items.example: He argued forcefully for the repair fund.
items.exampleCN: 他为维修基金展开了有力的论证。

items.meaning: to put force behind a rule
items.meaningCN: 把力量加在规则上；执行
items.example: Officers enforce the parking ban every morning.
items.exampleCN: 执法人员每天上午执行禁停规定。

items.example: Steel bars reinforce the concrete wall.
items.exampleCN: 钢筋加固了这面混凝土墙。

definition_zh: 运动；移动；动作；手势；动议；提议；机械运转；排便；用手势示意
definition_en: the act or process of moving, or a movement of the hand that signals something, or a formal proposal put to a meeting
core_image: 一枚棋子被手指从棋盘一格推到下一格，棋后拖出一道浅痕
scene: 会议开到一半，有人从座位上站起，把一页提案放到桌上，请全场表决。She rose to put a motion to the committee.
sceneCN: 这里 motion 指提交会议表决的正式提议（第 3 个义项：动议）；句意：她起身向委员会提出一项动议。图中可辨识物件：提案纸页、会议桌、木槌、座位牌。

pos.zh: 运动；移动；手势；动议；机械运转
用手势示意

senses.title: Change of position
senses.definition: the process of changing position or place over time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间改变位置或处所的过程
senses.example: The motion of the pendulum is regular and easy to time.
senses.exampleCN: 钟摆的运动很规律，容易计时。
senses.why: Latin motio is simply a moving, from movere 'to move'; this is the plainest and oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 motio 就是「移动」，出自 movere「移动」；这是最直白、最古老的义项。

senses.title: A gesture that carries a message
senses.definition: a movement of the hand or head used instead of words to signal something
senses.definitionCN: 代替言语、用来示意的手部或头部动作
senses.example: With a quick motion of his hand, the conductor silenced the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 指挥手一挥，大厅便静了下来。
senses.why: A gesture is a small movement that does the work of a sentence.
senses.whyCN: 手势是一个小动作，却承担了一句话的功能。

senses.title: A proposal put to a meeting
senses.definition: a formal proposal presented at a meeting for discussion and a vote
senses.definitionCN: 在会议上正式提出、供讨论并表决的提议
senses.example: The motion to extend the deadline was carried by nine votes.
senses.exampleCN: 延长截止日期的动议以九票通过。
senses.why: To bring something forward is to move it onto the table; the proposal is the thing set in motion before the room.
senses.whyCN: 把某事提出来，就是把它移到桌面上；提议就是被推到全场面前的东西。

senses.title: A request made to a court
senses.titleCN: 向法庭提出的程序申请
senses.definition: a formal request asking a court to make a ruling or take an action
senses.definitionCN: 请求法庭作出裁定或采取行动正式申请
senses.example: The defence filed a motion to dismiss the charge.
senses.exampleCN: 辩方提交了撤销指控的动议。
senses.why: A court, like an assembly, decides only what is moved before it, so the legal request kept the parliamentary name.
senses.whyCN: 法庭和议会一样，只裁决被推到它面前的事，因此法律申请沿用了议会里的名称。

senses.title: The act of starting a process
senses.definition: the act of setting a plan, process or event going
senses.definitionCN: 使计划、进程或事件开始运转的动作
senses.example: One phone call set the whole rescue in motion.
senses.exampleCN: 一个电话启动了整场救援。
senses.why: The fixed phrase set in motion treats a process as a body that must be pushed before it will move.
senses.whyCN: 「使……启动」这一固定说法把进程当作一具必须先推一把才会动的身体。

senses.title: The running of a machine
senses.definition: the working movement of a machine or mechanism, or its state of running
senses.definitionCN: 机器或机构的运转动作，或其正在运行的状态
senses.example: The old lift was in motion again after the belt was replaced.
senses.exampleCN: 换过皮带后，老电梯又运转起来。
senses.why: A machine is a body whose parts move, so its operation is naturally called motion.
senses.whyCN: 机器是一具有部件在动的身体，因此它的运行自然被叫作 motion。

senses.title: The moving works inside a device
senses.definition: the assembly of moving parts inside a device, especially a clock or watch
senses.definitionCN: 装置内部由运动部件组成的机构，尤指钟表机芯
senses.example: A watchmaker cleaned the motion and oiled each pivot.
senses.exampleCN: 钟表匠清理了机芯，并给每个轴心上了油。
senses.why: Watchmakers named the works by the movement they produce, and the term became the trade word for the whole mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 钟表匠以它所产生的运动来命名这套机构，这个说法后来成了整个机芯的行业词。

senses.title: To signal with the hand
senses.definition: to make a movement of the hand or head as a sign or direction
senses.definitionCN: 用手部或头部的动作作为信号或指引
senses.example: The usher motioned us toward the side door.
senses.exampleCN: 引座员示意我们往侧门走。
senses.why: The noun became a verb: to give a motion with the hand is to motion someone.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：用手给出一个动作，就是向某人示意。

intro.en: Motion comes through Old French from Latin motio, a moving, built on the past-participle stem mot- of movere 'to move'. The proposal sense grows from bringing something forward, not from physical travel.
intro.cn: motion 经古法语来自拉丁 motio「移动」，由 movere「移动、推动」的过去分词词干 mot- 构成。动议义由「把某事提出来、推到面前」引申，并非来自物理位移。

items.en: Movere meant to move, to push away, to set in motion; its past-participle stem mot- is the base of the noun.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、推开、使动起来；它的过去分词词干 mot- 是名词的底子。

items.en: Motio, motionis named a moving or a movement; it is a third-declension noun built on the same stem.
items.cn: motio、motionis 指一次移动或运动；这是由同一词干构成的第三变格法名词。

items.en: Old French motion carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first as movement and soon after as a proposal.
items.cn: 古法语 motion 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，先指移动，不久也指提议。

items.en: English motion is recorded from the fourteenth century in the plain sense of movement, and in legal use soon afterwards.
items.cn: 英语 motion 自十四世纪有「移动」的直白用法记录，随后不久进入法律语境。

items.en: The sense of a proposal grows from the idea of bringing something forward, a motion made in a room rather than in space.
items.cn: 「提议」义从「把某事提出来」这一想法长出，是在房间里而非空间中做出的动作。

items.en: The first dates of the parliamentary and legal senses are approximate; the noun is well attested from the medieval period.
items.cn: 议会义与法律义的最早记录年代为约数；这个名词在中世纪已有充分记录。

note.en: The first group shares the stem of moving; the second group separates motion from a gesture, a proposal and a trend.
note.cn: 第一组共享「移动」的词干；第二组把 motion 与手势、提议、趋势等相邻说法区分开。

entries.definition: The verb and a common noun for a single act of moving; motion is the more formal noun of the process.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，也作普通名词指一次移动；motion 是更正式、指整个过程的名词。

entries.definition: From mot- plus -ive: the reason that moves a person to act, not the act of moving.
entries.definitionCN: 由「移动」词干加表倾向的词尾构成：推动人去行动的理由，不是移动的动作。

entries.definition: Built on the same stem with an agent ending: the thing that produces movement, as an engine does.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词干加表施动者的词尾：产生运动的东西，如发动机。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus motion: a confused rushing about of people, a movement that is noisy.
entries.definitionCN: 表「一起」的拉丁前缀加「移动」：人群慌乱地涌动，一种喧闹的移动。

entries.definition: Not a form of motion and from a different source: it comes from a separate Latin noun for an instant or a weight, and in English it names a point in time rather than a movement.
entries.definitionCN: 不是 motion 的一种形式：它来自另一个拉丁名词，指瞬间或重量；英语中它指时间上的一点，而非移动。

entries.definition: Movement in general, often of a group or a trend; motion is more often a single act or a formal proposal.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指运动，常指一群人的行动或趋势；motion 更常指单次动作或正式动议。

entries.definition: A deliberate movement of the body that communicates; motion can be any movement, gesture is always meaningful.
entries.definitionCN: 有传达作用的身体动作；motion 可以是任何动作，gesture 一定带有意义。

entries.definition: A plan offered for consideration; a motion is a proposal put formally to a meeting.
entries.definitionCN: 提出供考虑的计划；motion 是正式提交会议表决的提议。

entries.definition: The ability to move from place to place, used of animals and vehicles rather than of processes.
entries.definitionCN: 从一处到另一处移动的能力，多用于动物与交通工具，而非抽象过程。

entries.definition: The speed at which something moves; motion names the fact of moving, not how fast.
entries.definitionCN: 移动的快慢；motion 说的是「在动」这件事，不涉及快慢。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Movere is Latin for move, and mot- is its participle stem.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语「移动」，mot- 是它的分词词干。

normal.en: The family runs motion, motionless, motive, motor, commotion.
normal.cn: 同族词有 motion、motionless、motive、motor、commotion。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the everyday senses: in motion, slow motion, set in motion, motion picture.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出日常义：在运动中、慢动作、启动、电影。

normal.en: Law says a motion to dismiss is a formal request, not a physical move.
normal.cn: 法律上的「撤销动议」是正式申请，不是物理移动。

normal.en: Physics describes motion with velocity and acceleration, two ways of measuring how it changes.
normal.cn: 物理用速度与加速度描述运动，这是衡量它如何变化的两种方式。

abstract.en: Picture a chess piece sliding one square, leaving a pale trail behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚棋子滑过一格，身后留下一道浅痕。

abstract.en: Picture a hand lifted at a meeting, and the room falling silent before a word is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象会议上一只手抬起，还没开口，全场就静了。

abstract.en: Picture a key turned in a lock and a whole machine waking up.
abstract.cn: 想象钥匙在锁里一转，整台机器醒了过来。

examples.en: The motion of the tide is charted twice a day.
examples.cn: 潮水的运动每天被记录两次。

examples.en: Her motion to reopen the case was rejected.
examples.cn: 她要求重审此案的动议被驳回了。

examples.en: The camera records motion in the dark by sensing heat.
examples.cn: 这台摄像机在黑暗中靠感热来记录运动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mo（摸）+ tion（神）」——摸一下就走，身子一动；motion 运动、动议

root: 拉丁 movere「移动、推动」→ 过去分词词干 mot- → 拉丁 motio「移动」→ 古法语 motion → 英语 motion；会议动议义由「提出、推动」引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one push: a body changes place, a hand makes a sign, an idea is pushed before a meeting, a request before a court, a process is started, a machine runs, its works are named, and finally the hand itself becomes a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「推」展开：身体换位、手做出信号、想法被推到会议前、申请被推到法庭前、进程被启动、机器运转、机芯得名，最后手本身变成动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger pushes a piece from one square to the next, and the piece leaves a trail.
core.cn: 核心意象：手指把棋子从一格推到下一格，棋子拖出一道痕迹。

branches.en: THE PLAIN MOVE: a body changes place, and one small move of the hand carries a message.
branches.cn: 直白的动：身体换位，而手的一个小动作传达信息。

branches.en: BROUGHT BEFORE OTHERS: the same push places a proposal before a meeting or a request before a court.
branches.cn: 推到众人面前：同一个推力把提议放到会议前，或把申请放到法庭前。

branches.en: SET GOING: a process is pushed into motion, and a machine keeps moving once it starts.
branches.cn: 使之启动：进程被推入运动，机器一旦启动便持续运转。

branches.en: THE WORKS: the parts that carry the movement inside a watch take the name of movement itself.
branches.cn: 机芯：钟表内部承担运动的那套部件，直接以「运动」命名。

branches.en: THE VERB: the hand that made the sign becomes the act of motioning.
branches.cn: 动词：做出信号的那只手，变成「示意」这个动作。

intro.en: Motion is a Latin noun of moving, and the stem mot- builds verbs, agents and a whole English family.
intro.cn: motion 是表示「移动」的拉丁名词，词干 mot- 还构成动词、施动者名词与整个英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere gives motio and motion, and also motive, motor, commotion and momentum; the ending -tion names an action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 movere 衍生 motio 与 motion，也衍生 motive、motor、commotion 与 momentum；后缀 -tion 表示动作或结果。

items.example: The root supplies the push behind every sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根为每个义项提供「推」的底子。

items.example: The Latin noun names the act of moving.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词指移动这一动作。

items.example: She rose to put a motion to the committee.
items.exampleCN: 她起身向委员会提出动议。

items.example: The cat lay motionless under the chair.
items.exampleCN: 猫一动不动地躺在椅子下。

items.example: A commotion broke out at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 门口爆出一阵骚动。

items.meaning: a reason that moves a person
items.example: Curiosity was his only motive.
items.exampleCN: 好奇是他唯一的动机。

items.example: The motor turns the belt.
items.exampleCN: 电动机带动皮带。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀
items.example: The ending turns a verb of moving into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「移动」的动词变成名词。

latinEntries.meaning: to move, push, set in motion

definition_zh: 运动；移动；动作；社会运动；乐章；走势；调动；排便
definition_en: an act of changing position or place, or an organized group working for a shared aim, or a section of a musical work
core_image: 一队人举着同样的牌子从广场一端走到另一端，脚步连成一道推进的横线
scene: 广场上，人们举着同样的牌子从一端走向另一端，队伍越来越长，喊声连成一片。The movement began with a few students and soon filled the square.
sceneCN: 这里 movement 指有共同诉求的群体性运动（第 3 个义项：社会运动）；句意：这场运动从几名学生开始，很快站满了广场。图中可辨识物件：手写标语牌、扩音器、横幅、统一的袖标。

pos.zh: 运动；移动；动作；社会运动；乐章；走势

senses.title: Change of position
senses.definition: the act or process of changing position or place
senses.definitionCN: 改变位置或处所的动作或过程
senses.example: A slow movement of the shelf warned that the wall was settling.
senses.exampleCN: 架子缓缓移位，说明墙体在下沉。
senses.why: Movement is the native noun of the verb move, and its oldest sense is simply the fact of changing place.
senses.whyCN: movement 是动词 move 的本族名词，最古老的意思就是「换了地方」这件事。

senses.title: A single action of the body
senses.definition: one deliberate action or gesture, especially of the hand or body
senses.definitionCN: 一次有意的动作或姿态，尤指手或身体的
senses.example: With one movement she folded the letter and sealed it.
senses.exampleCN: 她一个动作就把信折好封上了。
senses.why: A process can be cut into single acts, and one of those acts is also called a movement.
senses.whyCN: 一个过程可以切成一个个单独的动作，其中一次也叫 movement。

senses.title: An organized campaign for a cause
senses.titleCN: 为某一诉求组织起来的社会运动
senses.definition: a group of people acting together over time to bring about a change in society or policy
senses.definitionCN: 一群人长期共同行动，以求改变社会或政策
senses.example: The movement for clean rivers spread from one town to the whole valley.
senses.exampleCN: 洁净河流的运动从一个镇扩展到整个河谷。
senses.why: In the nineteenth century people acting together were seen as one body on the move, so a campaign became a movement.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪，人们把共同行动的一群人看作一个在移动的整体，于是运动便成了一项社会运动。

senses.title: A section of a musical work
senses.titleCN: 长篇乐曲中的一个乐章
senses.definition: a self-contained part of a long musical composition, such as a symphony
senses.definitionCN: 长篇乐曲（如交响曲）中相对独立的一部分
senses.example: The second movement is slow and almost silent.
senses.exampleCN: 第二乐章缓慢而近乎无声。
senses.why: Music was thought of as advancing in stages; each stage is a movement within the whole work.
senses.whyCN: 人们把音乐想成一段段向前推进；每一个阶段就是整部作品里的一个乐章。

senses.title: A trend in figures or opinion
senses.definition: a change in level, price or opinion over time, seen as a direction
senses.definitionCN: 水平、价格或舆论随时间的变化，被看作一个方向
senses.example: The upward movement in rents began before the new bridge opened.
senses.exampleCN: 租金的上涨走势在新桥通车前就开始了。
senses.why: A line on a chart that keeps going one way looks like something travelling, so a trend is called a movement.
senses.whyCN: 图表上一直朝一个方向走的线，看起来像有东西在行进，因此趋势也被称为 movement。

senses.title: The mechanism inside a clock
senses.definition: the assembly of moving parts that drives a clock or watch
senses.definitionCN: 驱动钟表的整套运动部件
senses.example: The watch has a hand-wound movement and a glass back.
senses.exampleCN: 这块表是手上链机芯，背面是玻璃的。
senses.why: Watchmakers named the works by the movement they produce, and the term became the trade word for the whole mechanism.
senses.whyCN: 钟表匠以它产生的运动来命名这套机构，这个说法后来成了整个机芯的行业词。

senses.title: A relocation of troops or supplies
senses.definition: the organized moving of troops, ships or supplies from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 有组织地把部队、船只或物资从一处移到另一处
senses.example: Satellite images tracked the movement of trucks along the border.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星图像追踪了卡车沿边境的调动。
senses.why: A body of men or goods changing place is still the plain sense, made formal by military use.
senses.whyCN: 一批人或货物换地方，仍是那个直白的意思，只是被军事用法正式化了。

senses.title: A bowel movement
senses.definition: an act of emptying the bowels, used as a neutral medical term
senses.definitionCN: 排空肠道的一次动作，用作中性的医学说法
senses.example: The nurse recorded the patient's movements after surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 护士记录了病人术后的排便情况。
senses.why: Medicine needed a plain, polite noun for a bodily action, and the ordinary word for moving served.
senses.whyCN: 医学需要一个平实而礼貌的词来指这一身体动作，于是用了「移动」这个普通词。

intro.en: Movement comes through Old French movement from movoir, the French form of Latin movere 'to move'. The musical and social senses are later growths from the plain idea of something advancing.
intro.cn: movement 经古法语 movement 来自 movoir，即拉丁 movere「移动」的法语形式。乐章义与社会运动义都是后来的引申，源自「某物在向前推进」这一朴素想法。

items.en: Movere meant to move, to set going, and it is the source of the whole French and English family.
items.cn: movere 意为移动、使动，是整个法语与英语词族的源头。

items.en: The French verb movoir or moveir meant to move and gave English the verb move.
items.cn: 法语动词 movoir 或 moveir 意为移动，并给英语带来了动词 move。

items.en: The noun movement named the act of moving; it uses the same action-noun ending as many French words in -ment.
items.cn: 名词 movement 指移动这一动作；它用的动作名词词尾，与许多以 -ment 结尾的法语词相同。

items.en: English took the noun in the fourteenth century, at first for physical movement and later for a single action.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪引入这个名词，起初指物理移动，后来也指单次动作。

items.en: From the eighteenth century a movement named a section of a symphony or sonata, following the idea of music advancing by stages.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，movement 指交响曲或奏鸣曲中的一个部分，沿用「音乐分段推进」的想法。

items.en: The collective sense for a campaign is a nineteenth-century growth, when large groups acting for a cause were described as one moving body.
items.cn: 指社会运动的集体义是十九世纪长出的，当时为某一诉求行动的大群人是被当作一个移动的整体来描述。

note.en: The first group shares the verb move and is often mistaken for the noun; the second group separates movement from motion, campaign and trend.
note.cn: 第一组共享动词 move，常与这个名词混淆；第二组把 movement 与 motion、campaign、trend 等词区分开。

entries.definition: The verb and a countable noun for one act of moving; movement is the noun of the process or the campaign.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，也可数名词指一次移动；movement 指过程或社会运动。

entries.definition: Move plus -able: able to be moved, said of furniture or a feast day; it is an adjective, not an act.
entries.definitionCN: 由动词加表「能够」的词尾构成：可被移动的，用于家具或不固定的节期；是形容词，不是动作。

entries.definition: Move plus -ing: either in the act of moving or able to stir the feelings, as a moving speech does.
entries.definitionCN: 由动词加表进行或性质的词尾构成：或指正在移动，或指能打动人心，如感人的演讲。

entries.definition: A shortened form of moving picture, from the moving images on film; it is a thing, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 「活动影像」一词的缩略，来自胶片上移动的影像；指作品，不是动作。

entries.definition: Move plus -er: a person or thing that moves something, or a company that transports goods.
entries.definitionCN: 由动词加表施动者的词尾构成：推动某事的人或物，也指搬家公司。

entries.definition: Often a single physical act or a formal proposal; movement is wider and covers campaigns and trends.
entries.definitionCN: 多指单次物理动作或正式动议；movement 范围更宽，还涵盖社会运动与趋势。

entries.definition: An organized series of actions for a goal; a movement is broader and longer, and usually social.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目标组织的一系列行动；movement 更宽、更久，通常带社会性。

entries.definition: A strong effort or campaign to reach a target, often official; it stresses the push, not the people.
entries.definitionCN: 为达目标的有力推动或活动，常是官方发起的；强调推动力，不强调人群。

entries.definition: The general direction in which something is changing; movement can name a change in figures but is more concrete.
entries.definitionCN: 事物变化的总方向；movement 也能指数字变动，但更具体。

entries.definition: The ability to move from place to place, used of animals and vehicles; it is technical and not social.
entries.definitionCN: 从一处到另一处移动的能力，用于动物和交通工具；属技术用语，不含社会义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Movere is Latin for move, and movement is the noun made from the French verb.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语「移动」，movement 是由法语动词变来的名词。

normal.en: The family runs move, movable, moving, movie, mover.
normal.cn: 同族词有 move、movable、moving、movie、mover。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: social movement, slow movement, upward movement.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：社会运动、慢乐章、上升走势。

normal.en: The -ment ending turns an action into a noun, as in agreement and management.
normal.cn: 名词词尾把动作变成名词，如「同意」与「管理」二词。

normal.en: A clock's movement is the works that keep it moving, a trade term from watchmaking.
normal.cn: 钟表的 movement 是让它持续运转的机芯，这是制表业的行业说法。

abstract.en: Picture one person walking, then a hundred walking in the same direction.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人走，然后一百个人朝同一个方向走。

abstract.en: Picture a symphony advancing one stage at a time, each stage its own room.
abstract.cn: 想象一部交响曲一段段向前走，每个阶段自成一间屋子。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a graph climbing and someone calling that climb a movement.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上一条线往上爬，有人把这段爬升叫 movement。

examples.en: The movement of goods across the border slowed after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，货物过境的流动变慢了。

examples.en: The civil rights movement changed the town's hiring rules.
examples.cn: 民权运动改变了这座小镇的用工规定。

examples.en: A thermostat senses the movement of air through the duct.
examples.cn: 恒温器感知空气在管道中的流动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「move（挪）+ ment（门特）」——挪一挪，人群就成了一场运动；movement 移动、运动、乐章

root: 拉丁 movere「移动」→ 古法语 movoir「移动」→ 古法语名词 movement「移动、动作」→ 英语 movement；乐章义由乐曲内部的推进，社会运动义为十九世纪集体行动的用法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one body in motion: it changes place, makes a single act, gathers into a campaign, advances as a section of music, climbs as a trend, drives a clock, moves as troops, and passes as a bodily function.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「在动的身体」展开：它换位、做出一次动作、聚成一场运动、作为乐曲的一部分推进、作为趋势上升、驱动机芯、作为部队调动，最后成为一种身体功能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of people walking together in one direction, their steps forming an advancing line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队人朝同一方向走，脚步连成一条推进的横线。

chain: A LINE ON A CHART RISES

branches.en: PLAIN MOVING: one body changes place, and one deliberate action of the hand is carved out of it.
branches.cn: 直白的动：一具身体换了地方，其中切出手的一次有意动作。

branches.en: PEOPLE TOGETHER: many bodies moving for one cause become a social movement.
branches.cn: 众人同行：许多身体为一个诉求而动，聚成社会运动。

branches.en: A WORK IN STAGES: music advancing by sections gives the musical movement its name.
branches.cn: 分段推进的作品：音乐按段落向前，乐章由此得名。

branches.en: A CLIMB ON A CHART: the same advance is read as a trend in figures.
branches.cn: 图表上的爬升：同一种推进被读成数字的走势。

branches.en: MOVING PARTS AND BODIES: a watch's works, a column of trucks, and the bowels all carry the plain sense into new settings.
branches.cn: 运动部件与身体：钟表机芯、车队与肠道，都把直白义带进新的场合。

intro.en: Movement is a French action noun built on the Latin verb of moving, with the same ending that forms many English nouns.
intro.cn: movement 是一个由拉丁「移动」动词构成的法语动作名词，用的词尾也构成许多英语名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere gives move, motion, motive and motor; the French noun movement adds the action-noun ending to the same verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 movere 衍生 move、motion、motive 与 motor；法语名词 movement 则在同一个动词上加动作名词词尾。

items.example: The verb supplies the push behind every sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词为每个义项提供「推」的底子。

items.example: The French verb passed into English as move.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语动词进入英语后成为 move。

items.meaning: the act of moving; a campaign
items.example: The movement began with a few students.
items.exampleCN: 这场运动从几名学生开始。

items.example: The machine's movements are smooth and silent.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器的各个动作平顺而安静。

items.meaning: to shift; to touch the feelings
items.example: Move the chair closer to the window.
items.exampleCN: 把椅子挪近窗户一些。

items.example: The stage has a movable floor.
items.exampleCN: 这个舞台有一块可移动的地板。

items.example: It was a moving account of the flood.
items.exampleCN: 那是对洪水的感人叙述。

items.example: The movie ran for two hours.
items.exampleCN: 这部电影放映了两个小时。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词后缀
items.example: It is the same ending as in management and agreement.
items.exampleCN: 它与 management 和 agreement 用的是同一个词尾。

latinEntries.meaning: to move, push, set in motion

definition_zh: 速度；速率；速度矢量；快速；周转速度
definition_en: the speed of something in a given direction, or the rate at which something moves or changes
core_image: 一支箭离弦后，箭头旁画着一条带箭头的直线，线上标着等距刻度
scene: 实验台上，小车沿倾斜导轨滑下，两道光门依次亮起，计时器记下通过的时刻。The sensor measured the cart's velocity as it passed each gate.
sceneCN: 这里 velocity 指物体在某一方向上的运动快慢（第 1 个义项：带方向的速度矢量）；句意：传感器测出小车经过每道光门时的速度。图中可辨识物件：倾斜导轨、小车、光门、计时器。

pos.zh: 速度；速率；速度矢量；快速；周转速度

senses.title: Speed with a direction
senses.definition: the rate at which an object changes position, measured as distance divided by time and stated with a direction
senses.definitionCN: 物体位置改变的速率，以距离除以时间计量，并标明方向
senses.example: Velocity differs from speed in that it must include a direction.
senses.exampleCN: 速度与速率的不同在于，速度必须包含方向。
senses.why: Physicists needed a word for speed tied to a direction, and Latin velocitas supplied the plain word for swiftness.
senses.whyCN: 物理学家需要一个词来表示与方向绑定的快慢，拉丁 velocitas 正好提供了「迅速」这个朴素的词。

senses.title: Swiftness in everyday speech
senses.definition: the speed at which something moves, without the technical idea of direction
senses.definitionCN: 某物移动的快慢，不带方向这一技术含义
senses.example: The train gathered velocity as it left the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 火车驶出山谷时越来越快。
senses.why: Outside the laboratory the direction is often left out, so velocity simply means high speed.
senses.whyCN: 出了实验室，方向常被略去，velocity 就单纯指「快」。

senses.title: Rate of a change or process
senses.definition: the rate at which a process or quantity changes over time
senses.definitionCN: 某一过程或数量随时间变化的快慢
senses.example: The velocity of the reaction fell as the mixture cooled.
senses.exampleCN: 混合物冷却后，反应速率下降了。
senses.why: Velocity measures how fast a distance grows; any quantity that grows at a steady rate can take the same word.
senses.whyCN: velocity 衡量距离增长得多快；任何按稳定速率增长的量，都能用同一个词。

senses.title: The circulation rate of money
senses.definition: the average number of times money changes hands in an economy over a period
senses.definitionCN: 一定时期内货币在经济中平均转手的次数
senses.example: A higher velocity of money can raise prices without more cash.
senses.exampleCN: 货币流通速度提高，不必增加现金也能推高物价。
senses.why: Economists treat money as a body in motion: the faster it passes from hand to hand, the higher its velocity.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把钱看作在运动的东西：它转手越快，速度就越高。

senses.title: The speed of a projectile
senses.definition: the speed of a bullet, shell or thrown object at a stated point in its flight
senses.definitionCN: 子弹、炮弹或抛射物在飞行中某一指定点的速度
senses.example: The muzzle velocity of the rifle was recorded for every batch.
senses.exampleCN: 每一批步枪的出膛速度都有记录。
senses.why: Gunners measured how fast a shot leaves the barrel and called that measured speed its velocity.
senses.whyCN: 炮手测量弹丸离膛多快，并把这一测得的速度称作它的 velocity。

senses.title: The rate of rotation
senses.definition: the rate at which an object turns about an axis, usually given in radians per second
senses.definitionCN: 物体绕轴旋转的速率，通常以每秒弧度表示
senses.example: The wheel's angular velocity doubled when the load was removed.
senses.exampleCN: 卸去负载后，轮子的角速度加倍。
senses.why: Turning is motion around an axis, so the same measuring word was applied to angles rather than to straight distance.
senses.whyCN: 转动是绕轴的运动，于是同一个测量词被用到角度上，而不是直线距离上。

senses.title: The steady speed of a falling body
senses.definition: the constant speed reached when the force of gravity is balanced by air resistance
senses.definitionCN: 重力与空气阻力相平衡时达到的恒定速度
senses.example: A falling raindrop reaches terminal velocity within a few metres.
senses.exampleCN: 雨滴落下几米就达到收尾速度。
senses.why: When a falling body stops speeding up, its velocity has become steady, and the phrase names that end point.
senses.whyCN: 当落体不再加速，它的速度就稳定了，这个说法指的就是那个终点。

senses.title: The speed of light
senses.definition: the constant speed at which light travels in a vacuum, about three hundred million metres per second
senses.definitionCN: 光在真空中传播的恒定速度，约为每秒三亿米
senses.example: The velocity of light sets the limit for every signal we send.
senses.exampleCN: 光速为我们发出的每一个信号设定了上限。
senses.why: The speed of light became the fixed reference speed of physics, so it is called the velocity of light.
senses.whyCN: 光速成了物理学的固定参考速度，因此被称为「光的 velocity」。

intro.en: Velocity comes from Latin velocitas, swiftness, built on velox 'swift'. It entered English in the seventeenth century as mechanics began to measure motion, but the deeper origin of velox is unsettled.
intro.cn: velocity 来自拉丁 velocitas「迅速」，由 velox「快」构成。它在十七世纪随力学开始定量测量运动而进入英语，但 velox 的更深来源没有定论。

items.en: Velox meant swift or quick; it described horses, runners and anything that moves fast.
items.cn: velox 意为迅捷、快；可形容马、奔跑者以及任何动得快的东西。

items.en: Velocitas, built on velox, was the noun for swiftness, used of bodies and of the passing of time.
items.cn: velocitas 由 velox 构成，是表示「迅速」的名词，用于物体，也用于时间的流逝。

items.en: English borrowed velocity in the seventeenth century, when mechanics began to measure motion numerically.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 velocity，当时力学开始用数字测量运动。

items.en: The vector sense, speed tied to a direction, became standard in physics teaching in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 把快慢与方向绑定的矢量义，在十九世纪的物理教学中成为标准。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of velox is not established. A link with vehere 'to carry' has been suggested but not demonstrated, so no Indo-European root should be asserted.
items.cn: 来源不确定：velox 的更深来源未得到确认。有人提出它与 vehere「运送」有关，但未获证实，因此不应断言某个印欧词根。

items.en: The first dates for the technical and economic senses are approximate; the word itself is well recorded from the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 技术义与经济义的最早记录年代为约数；这个词本身在十七世纪已有充分记录。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin word for swift or merely rhymes with velocity; the second group separates velocity from speed, rate and momentum.
note.cn: 第一组或共享那个表示「快」的拉丁词，或只是与 velocity 音近；第二组把 velocity 与 speed、rate、momentum 区分开。

entries.definition: A rare adjective from Latin velox, meaning swift; it describes the quality, not a measured quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁 velox 而来的罕用形容词，意为迅疾；描述性质，不是可测的量。

entries.definition: An early pedal or hand-cranked vehicle; from Latin velox plus pes 'foot', so it means swift-footed.
entries.definitionCN: 早期的脚踏或手摇车辆；由拉丁 velox 加 pes「脚」构成，意为「快脚」。

entries.definition: A track for cycle racing; its first part goes back through French vélo to velocipede, and so to velox.
entries.definitionCN: 自行车赛道；前半部分经法语 vélo 上溯到 velocipede，再上溯到 velox。

entries.definition: From Latin verax 'truthful', built on verus 'true'; it looks like velocity but has nothing to do with speed.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 verax「诚实的」，由 verus「真」构成；形似 velocity，却与速度无关。

entries.definition: From Latin vorax 'greedy', built on vorare 'to devour'; another word in -acity that only sounds like velocity.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 vorax「贪食的」，由 vorare「吞食」构成；又一个只在读音上像 velocity 的词。

entries.definition: The distance covered per unit time without direction; velocity adds direction and is a vector.
entries.definitionCN: 单位时间内走过的距离，不带方向；velocity 加上方向，是矢量。

entries.definition: The rate of movement, often of walking or of a repeated action; it is less technical than velocity.
entries.definitionCN: 移动的快慢，常指走路或重复动作的节奏；不如 velocity 技术化。

entries.definition: A measure of change per unit of time; velocity is a particular rate applied to position.
entries.definitionCN: 单位时间内的变化量；velocity 是这一量用在位置上的特例。

entries.definition: Mass multiplied by velocity; it measures the push a moving body can deliver, not its speed alone.
entries.definitionCN: 质量乘以速度；衡量运动物体能给出的推力，不只是快慢。

entries.definition: The rate at which velocity itself changes; it is the slope of a velocity graph, not the speed.
entries.definitionCN: 速度本身变化的快慢；是速度图线的斜率，不是速度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Velox is Latin for swift, and velocitas is swiftness.
normal.cn: velox 是拉丁语「快」，velocitas 就是「迅速」。

normal.en: The family runs velocity, velocities, velocious, velocimeter, velocimetry.
normal.cn: 同族词有 velocity、velocities、velocious、velocimeter、velocimetry。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical senses: average velocity, angular velocity, terminal velocity, velocity of money.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术义：平均速度、角速度、收尾速度、货币流通速度。

normal.en: Physics keeps the difference: velocity is a vector, speed is its size.
normal.cn: 物理守住这个区别：velocity 是矢量，speed 是它的大小。

normal.en: Guns and economics both use it: muzzle velocity for a shot, velocity of money for spending.
normal.cn: 枪炮与经济学都用它：弹丸讲出膛速度，花钱讲货币流通速度。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow already in the air, a straight line drawn beside it with even ticks.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭已在空中，旁边画着一条带均匀刻度的直线。

abstract.en: Picture a needle on a dial climbing past every mark at once.
abstract.cn: 想象表盘上的指针一口气冲过所有刻度。

abstract.en: Picture a coin passing from hand to hand so fast it never rests.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币在人手间飞快传递，从不停下。

examples.en: The probe's velocity was calculated from two radar readings.
examples.cn: 探测器的速度由两次雷达读数算出。

examples.en: The cyclist held a steady velocity along the flat road.
examples.cn: 骑车人在平路上保持着稳定的速度。

examples.en: Economists watch the velocity of money as a sign of spending.
examples.cn: 经济学家把货币流通速度看作消费的迹象。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ve（微）+ lo（乐）+ city（城市）」——一路乐着穿过城市，越走越快；velocity 速度

root: 拉丁 velox「快」→ 拉丁 velocitas「迅速」→ 英语 velocity；velox 的更深来源不确定，与 vehere「运送」的联系仅为假说，不作定论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one arrow: it carries a direction, flies fast in plain speech, measures any process, times the circulation of money, leaves a barrel, turns a wheel, settles into a fall, and finally limits every signal as the speed of light.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一支箭展开：它带着方向、在日常话里飞快、可量任何过程、计货币的流通、离膛而出、带动车轮旋转、在坠落中稳定下来，最后作为光速为一切信号设限。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an arrow leaves the bow, and a straight line with even ticks is drawn beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：箭离弦而出，旁边画着一条带均匀刻度的直线。

branches.en: THE VECTOR: distance per time with a direction attached is the measuring core of the word.
branches.cn: 矢量：距离除以时间并附上方向，是这个词的测量核心。

branches.en: SPEED AND RATE: everyday speech drops the direction, and any growing quantity can borrow the same measure.
branches.cn: 快慢与速率：日常说话略去方向，任何增长的量也能借用同一测量。

branches.en: MONEY IN MOTION: economists count how fast cash passes from hand to hand.
branches.cn: 运动的钱：经济学家计算现金转手有多快。

branches.en: MEASURED MOTION: a shot, a spinning wheel and a falling drop are each given a velocity at a chosen point.
branches.cn: 被测量的运动：弹丸、转轮与落滴，各在选定的一点上给出速度。

branches.en: THE LIMIT: light travels at a fixed speed that no signal can exceed.
branches.cn: 上限：光以固定速度传播，任何信号都无法超过。

intro.en: Velocity is a Latin noun of swiftness, and its root builds a small family of measuring words in English.
intro.cn: velocity 是一个表示「迅速」的拉丁名词，它的词根在英语里构成一小族与测量有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin velox 'swift' gives velocitas and velocity, and also velocipede, velodrome and the rare velocious; the ending -ity forms nouns of quality.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 velox「快」衍生 velocitas 与 velocity，也衍生 velocipede、velodrome 与罕用的 velocious；后缀 -ity 构成表性质的名词。

items.example: The adjective supplies the idea of speed to the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词为整个词族提供「快」的意思。

items.example: The Latin noun names the quality of being swift.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词指「快」这一性质。

items.example: The sensor measured the cart's velocity.
items.exampleCN: 传感器测出了小车的速度。

items.example: The two velocities were averaged.
items.exampleCN: 两个速度值被取了平均。

items.example: A velocious current swept the boat downstream.
items.exampleCN: 一股迅疾的水流把小船冲向下游。

items.example: The velocimeter was fixed to the rail.
items.exampleCN: 速度计固定在导轨上。

items.example: Laser velocimetry mapped the flow.
items.exampleCN: 激光测速法绘出了流场。

items.example: The velodrome hosted the final sprint.
items.exampleCN: 自行车赛场承办了最后的冲刺赛。

items.meaningCN: 构成表性质名词的后缀
items.example: The ending turns an adjective of speed into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把表示快的形容词变成名词。

definition_zh: 动量；冲力；势头；推动力；干劲
definition_en: the force that keeps a moving body going, or the growing drive behind a process
core_image: 一块石球顺着斜坡滚下，越滚越快，身后的尘土被推开成一条直线
scene: 接力赛最后一棒交到手上时，队伍已经领先半步，看台上的人开始提前欢呼。The runner carried the team's momentum through the final bend.
sceneCN: 这里 momentum 指已经积起、还会继续往前推的势头（第 3 个义项：进程累积起来的推进势头）；句意为跑者带着队伍已有的势头跑过最后一个弯道。图中可辨识物件：接力棒、弯道标记线、看台栏杆、扬起的尘土。

pos.zh: 动量；冲力；势头；推动力；干劲

derivatives.zh: 重大的；影响深远的（同一拉丁词干加形容词后缀）
片刻的；短暂的（同一词干加表示持续的后缀）

senses.title: Quantity of motion in physics
senses.titleCN: 物理学中质量与速度相乘的动量
senses.definition: a physical quantity equal to the mass of a moving body multiplied by its velocity
senses.definitionCN: 运动物体的质量与其速度相乘所得的物理量
senses.example: The cart's momentum doubled when its speed doubled.
senses.exampleCN: 小车的速度翻倍时，它的动量也翻倍。
senses.why: Seventeenth-century mechanics needed a name for the amount of motion a body carries, and took the Latin word for movement itself.
senses.whyCN: 十七世纪的力学需要给物体携带的「运动量」一个名字，于是直接取用了拉丁语中表示「运动」的那个词。

senses.title: The carrying force of a moving body
senses.titleCN: 运动物体带着向前冲的力量
senses.definition: the push that a moving body carries and that keeps it going until something stops it
senses.definitionCN: 运动物体所携带、并使其在受阻前持续前进的推力
senses.example: The loaded truck's momentum carried it through the intersection.
senses.exampleCN: 满载卡车的冲力使它冲过了十字路口。
senses.why: Once the word named a quantity, speakers used it for the felt push of a heavy body that will not stop at once.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词被用来指一个量之后，人们又用它来指重物那种不能立刻停下的可感推力。

senses.title: A process gaining strength
senses.titleCN: 事情逐渐积累起来的推进势头
senses.definition: the increasing strength of a process or movement that makes it hard to stop
senses.definitionCN: 某项进程或运动不断增强、难以遏止的力量
senses.example: The campaign gained momentum after the first debate.
senses.exampleCN: 首场辩论之后，这场竞选势头渐起。
senses.why: A process that keeps advancing looks like a body that keeps rolling, so the physical word was carried over to social change.
senses.whyCN: 不断推进的进程看起来就像持续滚动的物体，于是这个物理词被移用到社会变化上。

senses.title: A driving force behind change
senses.titleCN: 推动变化发生的外部动力
senses.definition: a force or factor that drives change forward in a field or economy
senses.definitionCN: 在某一领域或经济中把变化向前推动的力量或因素
senses.example: Cheap rail gave the inland trade fresh momentum.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价的铁路给内陆贸易带来了新的动力。
senses.why: Here the word shifts from the thing moving to the force that sets it moving, a common reversal of cause and effect.
senses.whyCN: 这里词义从「在动的东西」转到「使它动起来的力量」，是因果位置常见的互换。

senses.title: Personal drive or energy
senses.definition: the energy and confidence that keep a person working toward a goal
senses.definitionCN: 使一个人持续朝目标努力的精力与信心
senses.example: She lost momentum after the first rejection letter.
senses.exampleCN: 收到第一封拒信后，她就泄了劲。
senses.why: The image of a rolling body was applied to a person's inner motion, so that drive could be gained or lost like speed.
senses.whyCN: 滚动物体的画面被用到人内心的运动上，于是干劲也像速度一样可以增减。

senses.title: The upper hand in a contest
senses.titleCN: 比赛中占据上风的势头
senses.definition: the advantage a team or player holds when events start to favour them
senses.definitionCN: 当局势开始偏向一方时，该队或该选手所占的优势
senses.example: The home team seized momentum in the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 主队在下半场掌握了势头。
senses.why: In sport the physical sense narrows to the side that is rolling forward while the other is trying to stop it.
senses.whyCN: 在体育中，这个物理义收窄为：一方正向前滚动，另一方则试图把它拦住。

senses.title: Directional strength in markets
senses.titleCN: 市场中价格延续原方向的动能
senses.definition: the tendency of a price or market to keep moving in the same direction
senses.definitionCN: 价格或市场倾向于沿同一方向继续运动的力量
senses.example: Traders watch for momentum before buying a currency.
senses.exampleCN: 交易员在买入某种货币之前会先看它的动能。
senses.why: Technical analysis borrowed the physics term because a rising price was treated as a body with inertia of its own.
senses.whyCN: 技术分析借用了这个物理词，因为上涨的价格被当作一个自带惯性的物体。

senses.title: The unstoppable course of history
senses.titleCN: 历史或改革难以阻挡的进程
senses.definition: the collective force that keeps a large historical change moving forward
senses.definitionCN: 使大规模历史变化持续前进的集体力量
senses.example: The momentum of reform survived two changes of cabinet.
senses.exampleCN: 改革的势头挺过了两次内阁更替。
senses.why: The largest rolling body speakers can imagine is history itself, so the word ends by naming a collective movement.
senses.whyCN: 人们能想象的最大滚动物体就是历史本身，于是这个词最终用来指一种集体运动。

intro.en: Momentum comes from Latin momentum 'movement, moving power', built on the stem of movere 'to move' with the noun suffix -mentum; the physics sense was fixed after the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: momentum 来自拉丁 momentum「运动、推动力」，由 movere「移动」的词干加名词后缀 -mentum 构成；物理的「动量」义在十七世纪以后固定下来。

items.en: Movere meant to move or set something in motion, and its stem mov- supplied the verb behind the noun.
items.cn: movere 意为「移动、使某物动起来」，它的词干提供了这个名词背后的动词。

items.en: Momentum named a movement, the power that produces movement, and also a brief moment of time.
items.cn: momentum 指一次运动、产生运动的力量，也指短暂的一瞬。

items.en: The suffix -mentum turned a verb stem into a noun of action or result, the same ending seen in monumentum.
items.cn: 后缀 -mentum 把动词词干变成表示动作或结果的名词，与 monumentum 用的是同一个词尾。

items.en: Mechanics adopted the word for the measured quantity of motion, mass times velocity, and that reading became standard.
items.cn: 力学采用这个词来指可测量的运动量，即质量乘速度，这一读法后来成为标准。

items.en: From the rolling body the word spread to campaigns, markets and personal energy, all of which can gain or lose speed.
items.cn: 从滚动物体出发，这个词扩展到竞选、市场与个人精力，这些事物都能加速或减速。

items.en: The earliest recorded dates for the separate senses are approximate; the Latin noun itself is well attested.
items.cn: 各义项的最早记录年代为约数；这个拉丁名词本身已有充分记录。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like momentum; the second group names neighbouring kinds of force and speed.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 momentum 相近；第二组是意思相邻的其他「力、速度」说法。

entries.definition: A point in time; it is a shortened form of the same Latin noun that gave momentum, not a derivative built from it.
entries.definitionCN: 指某一时刻；它是同一个拉丁名词经法语缩略而来，并不是由 momentum 加缀派生。

entries.definition: Weighty or important; built on moment with an adjective suffix, it has nothing to do with physical motion.
entries.definitionCN: 意为重大、要紧；由 moment 加形容词后缀构成，与物理运动无关。

entries.definition: Lasting only a moment; the suffix marks duration, not the carrying of motion.
entries.definitionCN: 意为只持续一瞬；后缀标的是时长，而不是携带的运动。

entries.definition: The general noun for moving or a concerted campaign; it lacks the idea of a measured quantity carried forward.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指移动或一场有组织的运动；它没有「被携带的可测量之量」这层意思。

entries.definition: A keepsake or reminder; it comes from Latin memento 'remember', a different root, and only looks like momentum.
entries.definitionCN: 指纪念品或提醒物；来自拉丁 memento「记住」，词根不同，只是形近。

entries.definition: A force that starts something moving; from Latin impetere 'to attack', a different root from movere.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物开始运动的力量；来自拉丁 impetere「攻击」，与 movere 不同源。

entries.definition: Speed in a stated direction; it measures how fast, while momentum also takes mass into account.
entries.definitionCN: 沿指定方向的速度；它只衡量快慢，而 momentum 还把质量算进去。

entries.definition: The forward push of an engine or a hand; it names the push itself rather than the quantity a body carries.
entries.definitionCN: 发动机或手向前的推力；它指推力本身，而非物体携带的量。

entries.definition: Inner energy or an organized effort; it sits closer to the personal sense than to the physical one.
entries.definitionCN: 内心的干劲或一场有组织的努力；比物理义更贴近个人层面。

entries.definition: A sudden push, or in physics the change of momentum; from Latin pellere, a root different from movere.
entries.definitionCN: 突然的一推，物理学中也指动量的变化；来自拉丁 pellere，与 movere 不同源。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Movere is Latin for to move, so momentum is the movement itself turned into a noun.
normal.cn: movere 是拉丁语「移动」，momentum 就是把「运动」本身变成名词。

normal.en: The family runs moment, momentary, momentous and movement, all from the same Latin stem.
normal.cn: 同族词有 moment、momentary、momentous 与 movement，都出自同一拉丁词干。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the everyday sense: gain momentum, lose momentum, gather momentum.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出日常义：获得势头、失去势头、积聚势头。

normal.en: The noun suffix -mentum is the same one heard in monumentum, a thing that brings something to mind.
normal.cn: 名词后缀 -mentum 与 monumentum 相同，后者指让人想起某事的事物。

normal.en: In school physics the quantity is written as mass times velocity, which is exactly momentum.
normal.cn: 学校物理里把这个量写成质量乘速度，那正是动量。

abstract.en: Picture a stone rolling down a slope, and the dust behind it standing in a straight line.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头顺坡滚下，身后尘土立成一条直线。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd already walking in one direction; nobody has to push it, it simply keeps going.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人已经朝同一个方向走，没人推，他们只是继续走。

abstract.en: Picture a flywheel so heavy that the whole workshop slows when someone switches it off.
abstract.cn: 想象一只极重的飞轮，有人关掉它时整间工坊都跟着慢下来。

examples.en: The flywheel stores momentum and smooths the engine's pulses.
examples.cn: 飞轮储存动量，使发动机的脉动变得平顺。

examples.en: The study measured how much momentum the debris carried after the impact.
examples.cn: 这项研究测量了碎片在撞击后携带了多少动量。

examples.en: Public support for the ban gained momentum after the drought.
examples.cn: 干旱之后，公众对这项禁令的支持势头渐起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摸门特姆」——摸到了门路，劲头就一路往前推

root: 拉丁 movere「移动」→ 词干 mov- 加名词后缀 -mentum → 拉丁 momentum「运动、推动力」→ 英语 momentum；物理「动量」义在十七世纪以后固定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses track one rolling body: a measured quantity, its carried push, a process speeding up, the force behind it, a person's inner drive, a team's upper hand, a market's direction, and history itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个滚动物体：可测量的量、它携带的推力、逐渐加速的进程、背后的推动力、个人的干劲、一队的上风、市场的方向，最后是历史本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy stone rolls downhill, faster and faster, pushing the dust aside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块沉重的石球顺坡滚下，越来越快，把尘土推向两边。

branches.en: THE MEASUREMENT: mass times velocity turns the picture of rolling into a number physics can use.
branches.cn: 可测量：质量乘速度把滚动的画面变成一个物理学能用的数字。

branches.en: THE PUSH FELT: the same body keeps going and shoves aside whatever stands in its way.
branches.cn: 可感的推力：同一个物体继续前进，把挡路的东西推到一边。

branches.en: A PROCESS OR A TEAM THAT IS ROLLING: social campaigns and sports sides both gain speed.
branches.cn: 滚动中的进程或队伍：社会运动与球队都会积累速度。

branches.en: WHAT SETS THINGS ROLLING: the word moves from the moving body to the force behind it, up to history.
branches.cn: 使事物滚动的东西：词义从滚动的物体转到它背后的力量，再扩大到历史。

branches.en: INNER AND MARKET MOTION: a person's drive and a price's direction are private versions of the same roll.
branches.cn: 内心与市场的运动：个人的干劲与价格的方向，是同一滚动的两种私密版本。

intro.en: Momentum is built from the Latin verb movere and the noun suffix -mentum, and the same verb supports several English words.
intro.cn: momentum 由拉丁动词 movere 与名词后缀 -mentum 构成，这个动词还支撑起若干英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere gives movement, moment, momentum and motive; the suffix -mentum is the same ending found in monumentum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 movere 衍生 movement（移动）、moment（时刻）、momentum（动量）与 motive（动机）；后缀 -mentum 与 monumentum 用的是同一个词尾。

items.meaning: to move; to set in motion
items.example: The verb supplies the whole image of something set rolling.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了「使某物滚动起来」的完整画面。

items.structure: stem of movere used before suffixes
items.example: The bare stem is what the noun suffix attaches to.
items.exampleCN: 名词后缀正是接在这个光秃的词干上。

items.example: It turns a verb of moving into a noun for the movement.
items.exampleCN: 它把表示移动的动词变成指该运动的名词。

items.example: The noun carries both the motion and the force behind it.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时带着运动与推动它的力。

items.structure: shortened from the same Latin noun through French
items.example: The old noun also meant a brief instant, which survives in moment.
items.exampleCN: 这个古老名词也指短暂的一瞬，这一义留在 moment 里。

items.meaning: the act of moving; a campaign
items.example: The English suffix repeats the function of the Latin one.
items.exampleCN: 英语后缀重复了那个拉丁后缀的功能。

items.example: The adjective speaks of consequence, not of speed.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词说的是分量，而不是速度。

items.example: The suffix limits the noun to a very short stretch of time.
items.exampleCN: 后缀把这个名词限定在极短的一段时间里。

items.example: The abstract noun names how short the moment is.
items.exampleCN: 这个抽象名词指那一瞬有多短。

items.example: It only looks like our word and belongs to the memory family.
items.exampleCN: 它只是形近，实际属于「记忆」那一族。

definition_zh: 惯性；惰性；迟钝；不愿改变的状态
definition_en: the tendency of a body to keep its state of rest or motion, and of people or institutions to resist change
core_image: 一辆熄了火的满载推车仍顺着原来的方向滑出很远，谁拉它都不肯先转向
scene: 实验台上一只小球被轻推后，离开斜面仍在桌面上直直滑行，直到边缘才停下。The ball's inertia kept it moving long after the push ended.
sceneCN: 这里 inertia 指物体在不受外力时维持原有运动状态的性质（第 1 个义项：物理学上的惯性）；句意为小球被推之后，推力已停，它仍靠惯性继续滑行。图中可辨识物件：小球、斜面、实验台边缘、计时器。

pos.zh: 惯性；惰性；迟钝；不愿改变

senses.title: The physical tendency to keep a state
senses.titleCN: 物理学上保持原有状态的总倾向
senses.definition: the property by which a body at rest stays at rest and a body in motion keeps moving unless a force acts on it
senses.definitionCN: 物体在不受外力时保持静止或保持原有运动状态的性质
senses.example: The ball's inertia kept it moving long after the push ended.
senses.exampleCN: 小球被推之后，推力已停，它仍靠惯性继续滑行。
senses.why: Latin inertia first meant idleness, and seventeenth-century physicists borrowed it for the laziness of matter, its refusal to change state on its own.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 inertia 最初指「懒散」，十七世纪物理学家借它来形容物质的「懒」——不肯自行改变状态。

senses.title: Inertia while at rest
senses.titleCN: 静止物体不愿自行启动的惯性
senses.definition: the resistance a stationary body offers to being set in motion
senses.definitionCN: 静止物体对被推动起来所表现出的抗拒
senses.example: The heavy door showed its inertia when the handle was pulled.
senses.exampleCN: 门把手被拉动时，沉重的门显出静止惯性的抗拒。
senses.why: A body at rest must be pushed before it moves, so the oldest and plainest form of the laziness of matter is rest.
senses.whyCN: 静止的物体必须先被推才会动，因此物质之「懒」最朴素的一种表现就是静止。

senses.title: Inertia while moving
senses.titleCN: 运动物体不愿自行停下的惯性
senses.definition: the tendency of a moving body to keep its speed and direction until something interferes
senses.definitionCN: 运动物体在受到干扰前保持速度与方向的倾向
senses.example: The sled's inertia carried it past the marked line.
senses.exampleCN: 雪橇的惯性让它滑过了标记线。
senses.why: Once a body is moving, the same refusal to change state appears as a refusal to stop or turn.
senses.whyCN: 物体一旦动起来，同一种「不肯改变状态」就表现为不肯停下或不肯转向。

senses.title: Moment of inertia in mechanics
senses.titleCN: 力学中衡量转动惯性的转动惯量
senses.definition: a quantity measuring how strongly a body resists a change in its rotation
senses.definitionCN: 衡量物体抵抗转动状态改变的物理量
senses.example: The engineers lowered the moment of inertia by moving the weight inward.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把配重往里移，从而降低了转动惯量。
senses.why: The resistance that works against a straight push has a turning counterpart, and the same word names it.
senses.whyCN: 抵抗直线推力的惰性有一个旋转的对应物，用的还是同一个词。

senses.title: Mental reluctance to act
senses.titleCN: 个人心理上不愿行动的惰性
senses.definition: a person's unwillingness to start or keep up an effort
senses.definitionCN: 一个人不愿开始或不愿持续付出努力的状态
senses.example: He wanted to exercise but could not overcome his inertia.
senses.exampleCN: 他想锻炼，却克服不了自己的惰性。
senses.why: The laziness of matter became a metaphor for the laziness of a mind that will not shift from its present state.
senses.whyCN: 物质的懒被用来比喻心思的懒：不愿从当前状态挪动。

senses.title: Institutional resistance to change
senses.titleCN: 机构自身不愿改变的惰性
senses.definition: the tendency of an organization or system to keep doing things as it always has
senses.definitionCN: 组织或制度倾向于照旧运转、不肯更改的习性
senses.example: Bureaucratic inertia delayed the new safety rules for years.
senses.exampleCN: 官僚惰性使新的安全规章拖了好几年。
senses.why: A large organization, like a heavy body, needs a strong outside force before it changes course.
senses.whyCN: 庞大的组织就像重物，需要很强的外力才会改变方向。

senses.title: Sluggishness or apathy
senses.definition: a lack of energy or movement, whether in a person, a market or a process
senses.definitionCN: 缺精力、缺动静的状态，可指人、市场或进程
senses.example: After the holiday the office sank into inertia.
senses.exampleCN: 假期过后，办公室陷入一片懒散。
senses.why: The older Latin sense of idleness never disappeared; it survives whenever the word describes mere sluggishness rather than a force.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中「懒散」的老义从未消失；当这个词指单纯的迟钝而非一种力时，用的就是那一层。

senses.title: Chemical inactivity
senses.definition: the quality of a substance that reacts very little with other substances
senses.definitionCN: 一种物质与其他物质极少发生反应的性质
senses.example: The chemical inertia of the gas makes it useful as a shield in welding.
senses.exampleCN: 这种气体的化学惰性使它适合在焊接中作保护气。
senses.why: A substance that will not enter into reaction is, in the same image, too lazy to move; chemistry borrowed the word from mechanics.
senses.whyCN: 不愿参与反应的物质，用同一个比喻来说就是「懒得动」；化学从力学借来了这个词。

intro.en: Inertia comes from Latin inertia 'lack of skill, idleness', formed from iners 'unskilled, inactive', which joins in- 'not' to ars 'skill'. The physical sense was given to it in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: inertia 来自拉丁 inertia「无技艺、惰怠」，由 iners「无技艺的、不活动的」构成，而 iners 是 in-「不」加 ars「技艺」；物理「惯性」义是十七世纪赋予的。

items.en: Ars meant skill, craft or art, and a person without it was thought of as clumsy and idle.
items.cn: ars 指技艺、手艺或艺术，没有这门手艺的人就被看作笨拙而闲散。

items.en: Iners joined in- 'not' to ars, giving unskilled, inactive, sluggish; it is the adjective behind both inertia and English inert.
items.cn: iners 以 in-「不」加 ars，表示无技艺的、不活动的、迟缓的；它既是 inertia 的形容词来源，也是英语 inert 的来源。

items.en: Inertia was the abstract noun of that adjective: lack of skill, idleness, the habit of doing nothing.
items.cn: inertia 是那个形容词的抽象名词：无技艺、懒散、无所事事的状态。

items.en: Seventeenth-century natural philosophers gave the word to matter's resistance to any change of motion.
items.cn: 十七世纪的自然哲学家把这个词赋予物质对任何运动改变的抵抗。

items.en: The old sense of idleness then returned through metaphor, first for sluggish people and later for slow institutions.
items.cn: 「懒散」的老义随后经比喻回归，先指懒散的人，再指行动迟缓的机构。

items.en: The exact first dates for each sense are approximate; the Latin noun and the adjective are well attested.
items.cn: 各义项的确切首见年代为约数；这个拉丁名词与形容词都有充分记录。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like inertia; the second group names neighbouring kinds of slowness and resistance.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 inertia 相近；第二组是意思相邻的其他「迟缓、抗拒」说法。

entries.definition: Inactive or chemically unreactive; it comes from the same Latin adjective iners, but it is an adjective, not the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指不活动的或化学上不活泼的；出自同一个拉丁形容词 iners，但它是形容词，不是这个名词。

entries.definition: Relating to inertia, as in inertial navigation; it is built directly from the noun with an adjective suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 指与惯性有关的，如惯性导航；由这个名词直接加形容词后缀构成。

entries.definition: First or at the beginning; it comes from Latin initium 'beginning', not from iners, and only looks similar.
entries.definitionCN: 指最初的、开头的；来自拉丁 initium「开始」，并非出自 iners，只是形近。

entries.definition: The ability to begin things or a first step; its root is initium 'beginning', unrelated to inertia.
entries.definitionCN: 指开创的能力或第一步；词根是 initium「开始」，与 inertia 无关。

entries.definition: Having no inertia, a technical adjective used of idealized systems in physics.
entries.definitionCN: 指无惯性的，是物理学中用于理想化系统的技术性形容词。

entries.definition: Slow, heavy movement; it describes the visible pace rather than a resisting force.
entries.definitionCN: 指缓慢沉重的移动；描述看得见的节奏，而非一种抗拒的力。

entries.definition: Lack of interest or feeling; it is emotional indifference, not physical resistance.
entries.definitionCN: 指缺乏兴趣或情感；是情绪上的漠然，不是物理上的抵抗。

entries.definition: A state of no growth or flow, used of water, trade or ideas.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有增长或流动的状态，用于水、贸易或思想。

entries.definition: An opposing force or refusal to yield; it names active opposition, while inertia names passive staying.
entries.definitionCN: 指对抗的力或不肯让步；它强调主动对抗，而 inertia 强调被动维持。

entries.definition: A dull, sleepy inactivity, often temporary and bodily.
entries.definitionCN: 指昏沉、想睡的不活动状态，常是短暂而身体性的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Ars is Latin for skill, and in- says not, so iners means without skill, hence idle.
normal.cn: ars 是拉丁语「技艺」，in- 表示「不」，所以 iners 意为「没有技艺」，引申为懒散。

normal.en: The family runs inert, inertial, inertly, inertness and inertialess.
normal.cn: 同族词有 inert、inertial、inertly、inertness 与 inertialess。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the everyday sense: overcome inertia, bureaucratic inertia, mental inertia.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出日常义：克服惰性、官僚惰性、心理惰性。

normal.en: In physics, inertia is matter's refusal to change its state without an outside force.
normal.cn: 在物理学中，惯性是物质在没有外力时不肯改变状态的性质。

normal.en: The adjective inert and the noun inertia come from the same Latin word, but initial does not.
normal.cn: 形容词 inert 与名词 inertia 同出一个拉丁词，而 initial 并非同源。

abstract.en: Picture a cart whose engine has died, still rolling down the same road because nothing has stopped it.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆熄了火的推车，因为没有东西拦住它，仍沿同一条路滑行。

abstract.en: Picture a heavy door that will not swing until someone leans on it with their whole weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇沉重的门，没人用全身重量去靠，它就不动。

abstract.en: Picture a filing cabinet that keeps every old form because no one has ever been told to throw one away.
abstract.cn: 想象一只档案柜，因为从没人被交代可以扔掉，旧表格一直存着。

examples.en: The spacecraft's inertia carried it past the intended orbit.
examples.cn: 航天器的惯性使它越过了预定轨道。

examples.en: The study found that institutional inertia, not cost, blocked the reform.
examples.cn: 研究发现，阻碍改革的是制度惰性，而不是成本。

examples.en: He pushed the heavy box and felt its inertia resist him.
examples.cn: 他推那只重箱子，感到它的惯性在抗拒自己。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因那事」——一想到那件事就懒得动，惰性上来了

root: 拉丁 ars「技艺」→ 加否定前缀 in- 成 iners「无技艺的、不活动的」→ 拉丁 inertia「惰怠」→ 英语 inertia；物理「惯性」义十七世纪起被赋予。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one refusal: matter will not change its state, whether at rest, in motion or in rotation; people, institutions and chemicals then repeat the same refusal in their own fields.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都围绕同一种「不肯」：物质不肯改变状态，无论静止、运动还是转动；随后人、机构与化学物质在各领域重复这种不肯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a loaded cart with a dead engine keeps rolling along the old road because nothing stops it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆熄了火的满载推车，因为没有东西拦住，仍沿旧路滑行。

branches.en: THE LAW ITSELF: the single property behind rest, motion and rotation is matter's refusal to change on its own.
branches.cn: 定律本身：静止、运动与转动背后是同一种性质，即物质不肯自行改变。

branches.en: TWO FACES OF THE SAME REFUSAL: a body at rest will not start, a moving body will not stop.
branches.cn: 同一种不肯的两面：静止的不肯启动，运动的不肯停下。

branches.en: THE TURNING COUNT: rotation has its own measure of resistance, the moment of inertia.
branches.cn: 转动的计量：旋转有自己的一套抵抗量度，即转动惯量。

branches.en: FROM MATTER TO PEOPLE: a lazy mind and a rigid office both behave like heavy bodies.
branches.cn: 从物质到人：懒散的心思与僵硬的机构，行为都像重物。

branches.en: MERE SLOWNESS AND INERT CHEMISTRY: the old sense of idleness survives, and substances that do not react are called lazy too.
branches.cn: 单纯的迟缓与惰性化学：懒散的老义留存下来，不发生反应的物质也被称作懒。

intro.en: Inertia is built from a negative prefix, the Latin noun for skill, and an abstract noun ending; the same root gives English inert.
intro.cn: inertia 由一个否定前缀、表示「技艺」的拉丁名词和一个抽象名词词尾构成；同一词根衍生出英语 inert。

latinIntro.en: Latin ars gives art, artisan and artificial; in- plus ars gives iners, and its noun inertia gives English inertia and the adjective inert.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ars 衍生 art（艺术）、artisan（工匠）与 artificial（人造的）；in- 加 ars 得 iners，其名词 inertia 衍生英语 inertia 与形容词 inert。

items.example: The prefix denies the skill named by the root.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀否定了词根所说的技艺。

items.example: The root image is a person who knows a craft.
items.exampleCN: 词根画面是一个懂手艺的人。

items.example: The adjective describes both a clumsy worker and a still body.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词既能形容笨手笨脚的人，也能形容静止不动的物体。

items.example: The noun first names a human failing, then a physical property.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词先指人的一种缺陷，再指一种物理性质。

items.example: Chemistry uses the adjective for gases that hardly react.
items.exampleCN: 化学用这个形容词指几乎不反应的气体。

items.example: The adjective describes frames and navigation that rely on inertia.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述依赖惯性的参照系与导航。

items.example: The adverb describes doing nothing at all.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词描述完全无所动作。

items.example: The noun names the quality rather than the physical quantity.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指性质，而不是那个物理量。

items.example: The suffix removes the very property the word names.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀恰好去掉了这个词所指的性质。

definition_zh: 摩擦；摩擦力；由摩擦产生的热与磨损；人与人之间的龃龉
definition_en: the resistance that arises when one surface moves against another, or the tension between people or groups
core_image: 两只手掌用力对着搓，掌纹之间冒出细碎的热与屑
scene: 两位同事为一份预算反复修改，会上说话越来越短。Friction between the two colleagues slowed the project to a crawl.
sceneCN: 这里 friction 指人与人之间不断擦碰而产生的紧张（第 5 个义项：人际间的龃龉）；句意为两位同事之间的摩擦使项目慢得几乎停住。图中可辨识物件：摊开的预算表、两支笔、半杯冷掉的茶、关着的会议室门。

pos.zh: 摩擦；摩擦力；龃龉；阻力

forms.label: 名词（摩擦音；由同一词根）

derivatives.zh: 摩擦音；摩擦音的（同一词根）

senses.title: The act of rubbing surfaces together
senses.titleCN: 两个表面相互擦过的动作
senses.definition: the act of two surfaces rubbing against each other while one or both move
senses.definitionCN: 一个或两个表面移动时相互擦过的动作
senses.example: The friction of the rope against the rail wore a groove in the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 绳子与栏杆的摩擦在木头上磨出一道沟。
senses.why: Latin fricare meant to rub, and its noun frictio named the rubbing itself before it named any force.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 fricare 意为「摩擦」，其名词 frictio 先指「擦」这个动作，之后才指一种力。

senses.title: The force that opposes sliding
senses.titleCN: 阻碍两表面相对滑动的力
senses.definition: the force produced when two surfaces in contact move against each other and resist the motion
senses.definitionCN: 两个接触面相互移动时产生并阻碍该运动的力
senses.example: Engineers added a low-friction coating to the piston.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师给活塞加了一层低摩擦涂层。
senses.why: Once the rubbing was studied as a quantity, the noun shifted from the action to the resistance it produces.
senses.whyCN: 当人们把这种擦动当作一个量来研究，名词就从动作转到它所产生的阻力。

senses.title: Heat and wear from rubbing
senses.definition: the heat or damage that rubbing produces on a surface or between parts
senses.definitionCN: 擦动在表面或部件之间产生的热或损伤
senses.example: The friction of the drill bit scorched the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 钻头摩擦把木头烫焦了。
senses.why: Rubbing two things together makes them warm and wears them down, so the word came to name the effects as well as the cause.
senses.whyCN: 两物相互擦会发热并损耗，于是这个词既指原因，也指结果。

senses.title: A rasping sound of rubbing
senses.definition: the harsh sound made when rough surfaces are drawn across each other
senses.definitionCN: 粗糙表面相互擦过时发出的刺耳声响
senses.example: The friction of the bow on the strings filled the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 弓在弦上的摩擦声充满了大厅。
senses.why: The ear hears the rubbing as noise, which is the same event described through another sense.
senses.whyCN: 耳朵把这种擦动听成声响，这仍是同一件事，只是换了一个感官来描述。

senses.title: Tension between people
senses.definition: a feeling of tension or annoyance between people who rub against each other's habits
senses.definitionCN: 人们因习惯相互擦碰而产生的紧张或恼怒
senses.example: Friction between the two colleagues slowed the project to a crawl.
senses.exampleCN: 两位同事之间的摩擦使项目慢得几乎停住。
senses.why: Two people who irritate each other are pictured as surfaces scraping, and the eighteenth-century figurative use made this sense common.
senses.whyCN: 相互惹恼的两个人被想象成两个相擦的表面，十八世纪以后的比喻用法使这一义流行起来。

senses.title: Disagreement that slows work
senses.titleCN: 使事情办不下去的意见不合
senses.definition: disagreement over plans or terms that makes cooperation difficult and slow
senses.definitionCN: 在计划或条件上的分歧，使合作变得困难而缓慢
senses.example: There was friction over who would pay for the repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 在由谁出修缮费的问题上出现了摩擦。
senses.why: When talks scrape instead of glide, the image moves from private annoyance to a dispute that blocks a joint task.
senses.whyCN: 当谈判不再是顺畅滑行而是相擦，画面就从私人的恼怒转到挡住共同事务的争执。

senses.title: Resistance inside a system
senses.titleCN: 系统或流程内部消耗的阻力
senses.definition: anything in a process, market or machine that makes movement slower or costlier
senses.definitionCN: 流程、市场或机器中使运转更慢或代价更高的一切因素
senses.example: The app was designed to remove friction from the checkout.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用的设计目的是消除结账环节的阻力。
senses.why: Modern usage treats any drag in a flow as friction, borrowing the mechanical word for costs and delays.
senses.whyCN: 现代用法把流动中的任何拖拽都视为摩擦，用这个机械词来指成本与延误。

senses.title: Conflict between groups
senses.titleCN: 群体或阶层之间的冲突
senses.definition: repeated conflict or resentment between social groups that live or work in contact
senses.definitionCN: 接触密切的社会群体之间反复发生的冲突或怨气
senses.example: Friction between the two communities rose after the water shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 缺水之后，两个社群之间的摩擦加剧了。
senses.why: Communities that share a border rub against each other constantly, so the word widens from persons to whole groups.
senses.whyCN: 共享边界的社群不断相互擦碰，于是这个词从个人扩大到整个群体。

intro.en: Friction comes from Latin frictio 'a rubbing', from fricare 'to rub'; the deeper origin of fricare is uncertain, and the figurative sense for quarrels grew after the eighteenth century.
intro.cn: friction 来自拉丁 frictio「摩擦」，出自 fricare「摩擦、揉搓」；fricare 的更早来源不确定，指人际龃龉的比喻义是十八世纪以后长出来的。

items.en: Fricare meant to rub or chafe; its own earlier origin is uncertain, so no deeper root is claimed here.
items.cn: fricare 意为「摩擦、揉搓」；它更早的来源不确定，因此这里不声称更深的词根。

items.en: Frictio was the noun of that verb, naming a rubbing or the soreness left by it.
items.cn: frictio 是那个动词的名词，指一次摩擦或擦后留下的疼痛。

items.en: The word entered English through learned Latin and French, first as a term for rubbing and later for the resistance between surfaces.
items.cn: 这个词经学术拉丁语与法语进入英语，先指摩擦动作，后指表面之间的阻力。

items.en: Mechanics gave friction a measured place among forces, which fixed the physical sense of the word.
items.cn: 力学把摩擦列入可测量的力之中，固定了这个词的物理义。

items.en: Writers then applied the scraping image to quarrels and social life, producing the interpersonal sense.
items.cn: 随后作家把这种相擦的画面用到争吵与社交生活上，产生了人际义。

items.en: The first dates for the figurative senses are approximate; the mechanical sense is well recorded in the early modern period.
items.cn: 比喻义的最早年代为约数；机械义在近代早期已有明确记录。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like friction; the second group names neighbouring kinds of rubbing, drag and disagreement.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 friction 相近；第二组是意思相邻的其他「摩擦、阻力、不和」说法。

entries.definition: A part of a whole or a number below one; it comes from Latin frangere 'to break', a different root, and only sounds like friction.
entries.definitionCN: 指整体的一部分或小于一的数；来自拉丁 frangere「打破」，与 friction 不同源，只是音近。

entries.definition: A break in bone or rock; from Latin frangere 'to break', with no link to rubbing.
entries.definitionCN: 指骨头或岩石的断裂；来自拉丁 frangere「打破」，与摩擦无关。

entries.definition: A consonant made by forcing air through a narrow gap; the name comes from the same verb for rubbing.
entries.definitionCN: 指气流挤过窄缝发出的辅音；名称出自同一个表示摩擦的动词。

entries.definition: The adjective of friction, used of forces, heat and unemployment that arise from rubbing or drag.
entries.definitionCN: friction 的形容词，用于由摩擦或阻力产生的力、热与失业。

entries.definition: Invented writing; it comes from Latin fingere 'to shape or feign', not from the verb for rubbing.
entries.definitionCN: 指虚构作品；来自拉丁 fingere「塑造、假装」，并非出自那个表示摩擦的动词。

entries.definition: Wear or a scraped wound caused by rubbing on a hard surface.
entries.definitionCN: 因与硬面摩擦造成的磨损或擦伤。

entries.definition: Any force or refusal that opposes motion; friction is one specific mechanical kind.
entries.definitionCN: 指阻碍运动的任何力或抗拒；摩擦是其中一种具体的机械类型。

entries.definition: The resistance of air or water to a moving object, or anything that slows progress.
entries.definitionCN: 指空气或水对运动物体的阻力，也指拖慢进展的事物。

entries.definition: Strain between people or groups that may break into conflict.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或群体之间可能爆发为冲突的紧张。

entries.definition: Open disagreement and a lack of harmony, stronger and more audible than friction.
entries.definitionCN: 指公开的分歧与不和谐，比 friction 更强、更外显。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Fricare is Latin for to rub, so friction is rubbing before it is a force.
normal.cn: fricare 是拉丁语「摩擦」，所以 friction 首先是「擦」这个动作，然后才是一种力。

normal.en: The family runs frictional, frictionless, frictionally and the phonetic term fricative.
normal.cn: 同族词有 frictional、frictionless、frictionally 以及语音学术语 fricative。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the everyday sense: reduce friction, friction between, friction costs.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出日常义：减少摩擦、……之间的摩擦、摩擦成本。

normal.en: Physicists separate static friction, which holds a body still, from kinetic friction, which acts while it slides.
normal.cn: 物理学家把使物体停住的静摩擦与滑动时起作用的动摩擦区分开来。

normal.en: The deeper origin of fricare is uncertain, so no further root should be invented for it.
normal.cn: fricare 更早的来源不确定，不应为它编造更深的词根。

abstract.en: Picture two palms pressed together and rubbed hard until they feel warm.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手掌压在一起用力搓，直到发热。

abstract.en: Picture a stubborn drawer that screeches every time it is pulled.
abstract.cn: 想象一只倔强的抽屉，每次拉动都发出刺耳的响声。

abstract.en: Picture two people who agree on the plan but sigh at every sentence the other says.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人同意同一个计划，却对对方每句话都要叹一口气。

examples.en: Less friction in the bearing meant the motor ran cooler.
examples.cn: 轴承里的摩擦减少，意味着马达运转得更凉。

examples.en: The report blamed friction between agencies for the delayed response.
examples.cn: 报告把响应迟缓归咎于机构之间的摩擦。

examples.en: Repeated friction with the same neighbor can wear down a whole community.
examples.cn: 与同一邻居反复摩擦，会磨损整个社群。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗里克申」——两人一擦就生热，话不投机就起摩擦

root: 拉丁 fricare「摩擦、揉搓」→ 拉丁 frictio「摩擦」→ 英语 friction；fricare 更早的词源不确定，人际龃龉义是十八世纪后的比喻用法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one scrape: surfaces rub, the rub turns into a force, into heat and wear, into noise, then into the scrape between people, between plans, inside a system and between whole groups.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一次擦碰：表面相互擦过，擦动变成一种力，又变成热与磨损、声响，随后变成人与人、计划与计划、系统内部以及群体之间的擦碰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two palms pressed together and rubbed until they feel warm and gritty.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手掌压在一起用力搓，直到发热、发涩。

branches.en: THE SCRAPE ITSELF: before any force is named, the word simply describes two surfaces drawn across each other.
branches.cn: 擦本身：在指任何力之前，这个词只是描述两个表面相互擦过。

branches.en: THE FORCE MEASURED: the scrape becomes a quantity that engineers can reduce or use.
branches.cn: 被测量的力：擦动变成一个工程师可以减小或利用的量。

branches.en: WHAT THE SCRAPE LEAVES: warmth, wear and a harsh sound are the same event felt by skin and ear.
branches.cn: 擦动留下的东西：热、磨损与刺耳声，是同一件事被皮肤和耳朵感到的样子。

branches.en: BETWEEN PEOPLE AND PLANS: two habits scrape, and a shared task slows down.
branches.cn: 人与计划之间：两种习惯相擦，共同的任务就慢下来。

branches.en: SYSTEMS AND GROUPS: any drag in a flow, and any repeated conflict between communities, takes the same name.
branches.cn: 系统与群体：流动中的任何拖拽、社群间任何反复冲突，都用同一个名字。

intro.en: Friction is built from a Latin verb for rubbing and a noun ending, and the same verb supports several English words.
intro.cn: friction 由一个表示摩擦的拉丁动词和一个名词词尾构成，这个动词还支撑起若干英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fricare gives friction and the phonetic term fricative; the exact deeper source of fricare is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fricare 衍生 friction（摩擦）与语音学术语 fricative（摩擦音）；fricare 更早的确切来源不确定。

items.example: The verb gives the whole picture of two surfaces in contact.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给出两个表面相接触的完整画面。

items.structure: stem of fricare used before suffixes
items.example: The stem carries the action into the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干把动作带进名词里。

items.example: The ending turns the verb of rubbing into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把表示摩擦的动词变成名词。

items.example: The Latin noun first names the act, not a force.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词先指动作，而不是一种力。

items.example: The English noun later takes on the measured mechanical sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语名词后来承担了可测量的机械义。

items.example: The adjective is used of forces, heat and unemployment.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词用于力、热与失业。

items.example: The suffix describes a surface or a process with no drag at all.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀描述完全没有阻力的表面或流程。

items.example: The adverb names the manner in which something is driven.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词说明某物被驱动的方式。

items.example: Phonetics borrows the rubbing image for air forced through a gap.
items.exampleCN: 语音学借用了这个摩擦画面，指气流被挤过窄缝。

definition_zh: 吸引；吸引力；吸引人的事物；景点
definition_en: the power of drawing someone or something toward a person, place or thing, or the thing that draws them
core_image: 一枚磁石悬在铁屑上方，铁屑从四面立起，朝同一个点倾过去
scene: 海边小镇修好旧码头后，来往的车辆在路口排成长队，旅馆老板笑得合不拢嘴。The restored pier became the town's main attraction.
sceneCN: 这里 attraction 指把游客引来的地方（第 6 个义项：旅游景点）；句意为修葺一新的码头成了小镇最主要的景点。图中可辨识物件：旧码头、停满车的路口、旅馆招牌、手绘地图。

pos.zh: 吸引；吸引力；吸引人的事物；景点

forms.label: 复数（指多处景点或多种吸引力）

derivatives.zh: 吸引子；引人注意的人或物

senses.title: The act of drawing something near
senses.definition: the action or power of causing someone or something to come closer
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物靠近的动作或力量
senses.example: The attraction of iron filings to the magnet was immediate.
senses.exampleCN: 铁屑立刻被磁石吸了过去。
senses.why: Latin attrahere joined ad- 'toward' to trahere 'to pull', so attraction is literally a pulling toward.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 attrahere 以 ad-「向」加 trahere「拉」，所以 attraction 字面上就是「向这边拉」。

senses.title: Magnetic attraction
senses.definition: the force by which a magnet draws iron or another magnet toward it
senses.definitionCN: 磁体把铁或另一磁体拉向自己的力量
senses.example: The attraction between the two magnets closed the gap with a click.
senses.exampleCN: 两块磁体之间的吸引使缝隙咔嗒一声合上。
senses.why: The pulling-toward image is most visible in a magnet, so this became the clearest physical example of the word.
senses.whyCN: 「往自己这边拉」的画面在磁体上最明显，因此这成了这个词最清楚的物理实例。

senses.title: Gravitational attraction
senses.definition: the force that draws masses, such as planets, toward one another
senses.definitionCN: 把有质量的物体（如行星）相互拉近的力
senses.example: The attraction of the moon raises the tides twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 月球的引力每天两次抬起潮水。
senses.why: Once gravity was understood as a pull acting at a distance, the old verb for pulling was the natural name for it.
senses.whyCN: 当引力被理解为一种隔着距离起作用的拉，那个表示拉的老动词自然就成了它的名字。

senses.title: Personal or romantic attraction
senses.definition: a feeling of liking or desire that draws one person toward another
senses.definitionCN: 把一个人拉向另一个人的喜欢或爱慕之情
senses.example: Their attraction grew over a summer of shared shifts.
senses.exampleCN: 共同值了一个夏天的班，他们的好感渐渐生长。
senses.why: The physical pull was transferred to the pull one person feels toward another, the same inward direction.
senses.whyCN: 物理的拉被移用到一个人对另一个人的拉力，方向同样朝内。

senses.title: A fairground draw
senses.titleCN: 集市或游乐场里招人的项目
senses.definition: a ride or show provided to draw paying visitors to a fair or park
senses.definitionCN: 为把付费游客引到集市或乐园而设置的游乐项目或表演
senses.example: The giant wheel was the attraction that filled the fairground.
senses.exampleCN: 那座巨轮是让游乐场坐满人的招徕项目。
senses.why: By the nineteenth century the thing that did the pulling could be named by the pulling itself, so a ride became an attraction.
senses.whyCN: 到十九世纪，做「拉」这个动作的事物可以用「拉」本身来命名，于是游乐设施也成了 attraction。

senses.title: A tourist site
senses.definition: a place that visitors come to see, especially one promoted by a town or region
senses.definitionCN: 游客前来观看的地方，尤指由城镇或地区推介的
senses.example: The restored pier became the town's main attraction.
senses.exampleCN: 修葺一新的码头成了小镇最主要的景点。
senses.why: A place exerts the same pull on visitors as a magnet does on filings, so the sense widened from a show to a destination.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方对游客的拉力，就像磁石对铁屑，于是词义从表演扩大到目的地。

senses.title: The appeal of an idea or activity
senses.titleCN: 想法或活动本身的吸引力
senses.definition: the quality that makes an idea, job or activity interesting and desirable
senses.definitionCN: 使一个想法、工作或活动显得有趣而可取的品质
senses.example: The attraction of the job lay in its freedom, not its pay.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作的吸引力在于自由，而不在报酬。
senses.why: Abstract things also pull people toward them, and the word follows that pull into mental life.
senses.whyCN: 抽象事物也能把人拉过去，这个词便跟着这股拉力进入精神层面。

senses.title: The pulling of attention
senses.definition: the power of something to hold attention or draw a crowd
senses.definitionCN: 某物抓住注意力或引来人群的力量
senses.example: The speaker's calm voice had a quiet attraction for the whole room.
senses.exampleCN: 讲者平稳的声音对全场有一种安静的吸引力。
senses.why: Attention behaves like iron filings near a magnet: it turns toward whatever exerts the strongest pull.
senses.whyCN: 注意力就像磁石旁的铁屑：哪里的拉力最强，它就转向哪里。

intro.en: Attraction comes from Latin attractio, from attrahere 'to draw to', which joins ad- 'toward' to trahere 'to pull, drag'. The sense of a place or show that draws visitors is a nineteenth-century development.
intro.cn: attraction 来自拉丁 attractio，出自 attrahere「拉向」，由 ad-「向」加 trahere「拉、拖」构成；指景点或招徕项目的义项是十九世纪发展出来的。

items.en: Trahere meant to pull or drag something along behind oneself, the physical core of the whole family.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖」，把东西拽在自己身后，是整族词的物理核心。

items.en: The prefix ad- meant toward, so the compound described a pull directed at the speaker or the center.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 意为「向」，因此这个复合词描述一种朝向说话者或中心的拉。

items.en: Attractio named a drawing to or a gathering, the noun of the compound verb.
items.cn: attractio 是那个复合动词的名词，指「拉向」或「聚集」。

items.en: The word entered English in the late fourteenth century, first as a term for physical pulling and influence.
items.cn: 这个词在十四世纪晚期进入英语，最初指物理的拉与影响。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the word was applied to shows and sites that draw visitors, giving the modern travel sense.
items.cn: 十九世纪，这个词被用到招徕观众的表演与场所上，产生了现代的旅游义。

items.en: The first dates for the separate senses are approximate; the Latin noun is well attested.
items.cn: 各义项的最早年代为约数；这个拉丁名词有充分记录。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like attraction; the second group names neighbouring kinds of appeal and draw.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 attraction 相近；第二组是意思相邻的其他「吸引力、招徕」说法。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun: to pull someone or something toward oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词：把某人或某物拉向自己。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning having the power to draw people; it describes the quality, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 意为有吸引力的；它描述性质，而不是动作。

entries.definition: The grip that lets a wheel pull a vehicle forward; same Latin verb for pulling, a different use of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指让车轮拉着车辆前进的抓地力；同出那个表示拉的拉丁动词，用法不同。

entries.definition: Something that pulls attention away; the prefix means apart, the opposite direction from attraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指把注意力拉走的事物；前缀意为「分开」，方向与 attraction 相反。

entries.definition: An area of land or a pamphlet; from the same Latin verb, it names something drawn out or extended, not a pull toward a point.
entries.definitionCN: 指一片土地或一本小册子；同出那个拉丁动词，指被拉长、铺展开的东西，不是朝一点的拉力。

entries.definition: The quality of being pleasing or interesting enough to draw people; it stresses desirability.
entries.definitionCN: 指足以招徕人的讨喜或有趣之处，强调可取性。

entries.definition: A personal quality that delights others; it is warmer and more social than attraction.
entries.definitionCN: 指使他人愉悦的个人魅力，比 attraction 更温暖、更社交。

entries.definition: The physical property of magnets, or a strong personal draw felt as if by magic.
entries.definitionCN: 指磁体的物理性质，或一种仿佛有魔力般的强烈个人吸引力。

entries.definition: Something tempting used to draw someone in, often toward a risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指用来把人引来的诱饵，常带有风险意味。
