entries.definition: The power to pull a crowd; it is plainer and often used of audiences and events.
entries.definitionCN: 指招徕人群的力量，更朴素，常用于观众与活动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Trahere is Latin for to pull, and ad- means toward, so attraction is a pulling toward.
normal.cn: trahere 是拉丁语「拉」，ad- 意为「向」，所以 attraction 就是「向这边拉」。

normal.en: The family runs attract, attractive, attractively and attractiveness.
normal.cn: 同族词有 attract、attractive、attractively 与 attractiveness。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the everyday sense: tourist attraction, main attraction, magnetic attraction.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出日常义：旅游景点、主要看点、磁吸引。

normal.en: Gravity and magnetism are both described as attraction because both pull bodies toward each other.
normal.cn: 引力与磁性都用 attraction 来描述，因为两者都把物体相互拉近。

normal.en: The opposite of attraction in physics is repulsion, a push away from the same center.
normal.cn: 物理学中 attraction 的反面是 repulsion，即从同一个中心往外推。

abstract.en: Picture iron filings standing up and leaning toward a magnet like grass in wind.
abstract.cn: 想象铁屑立起来朝磁石倾斜，像风中的草。

abstract.en: Picture a lit window at the end of a dark street, and every walker turns toward it.
abstract.cn: 想象暗街尽头有一扇亮着的窗，每个行人都朝它转过去。

abstract.en: Picture a small town where the repaired pier becomes the reason buses stop.
abstract.cn: 想象一座小镇，修好的码头成了巴士愿意停下的理由。

examples.en: The gravitational attraction between the two stars keeps them in orbit.
examples.cn: 两颗恒星之间的引力使它们留在轨道上。

examples.en: The museum's new wing proved a strong attraction for school groups.
examples.cn: 博物馆的新展区对学生团体很有吸引力。

examples.en: Researchers studied the attraction of pollinators to different flower colors.
examples.cn: 研究者研究了传粉昆虫对不同花色的趋附。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊，拽克身」——看到好东西，忍不住被拽过去

root: 拉丁 trahere「拉、拖」→ 加 ad-「向」成 attrahere「拉向」→ 拉丁 attractio「拉向、聚集」→ 英语 attraction；景点义为十九世纪用法。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pull: a magnet draws iron, gravity draws planets, a person draws another person, a ride draws a crowd, a pier draws tourists, an idea draws interest, and attention itself leans toward the strongest pull.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一个拉力：磁石吸铁、引力拉行星、人吸引人、游乐项目招人、码头引来游客、想法引来兴趣，注意力本身也朝拉力最强处倾斜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: iron filings stand up and lean toward a magnet held above them.
core.cn: 核心意象：铁屑立起来，朝悬在上方的磁石倾过去。

branches.en: THE PULL ITSELF: the bare act of causing something to come closer, before any field of physics is named.
branches.cn: 拉本身：使某物靠近的单纯动作，尚未指任何物理领域。

branches.en: FIELDS THAT PULL: magnetism and gravity are the two clearest physical versions of the same toward-pull.
branches.cn: 会拉的场：磁与引力是同一种「向里拉」最清楚的两个物理版本。

branches.en: PERSON TO PERSON: liking and desire repeat the inward pull between two bodies.
branches.cn: 人对人：喜欢与爱慕重复了两个身体之间的向内拉力。

branches.en: THINGS AND PLACES THAT DRAW: a ride or a pier becomes the attraction because it does the pulling.
branches.cn: 会招人的事物与地方：游乐项目或码头之所以成为景点，是因为它在做「拉」这件事。

branches.en: IDEAS AND ATTENTION: abstract appeal and the turning of a gaze are the last, lightest forms of the same pull.
branches.cn: 想法与注意力：抽象的吸引力与被牵过去的目光，是同一种拉力最轻的形态。

intro.en: Attraction is built from a Latin verb for pulling and the prefixes and suffixes that turn it into a noun of drawing toward.
intro.cn: attraction 由表示「拉」的拉丁动词，以及把它变成「拉向」名词的前后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere gives traction, tractor, extract, distract and attract; ad- plus trahere gives attrahere, and its noun attractio gives English attraction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 trahere 衍生 traction（牵引）、tractor（拖拉机）、extract（抽出）、distract（分心）与 attract（吸引）；ad- 加 trahere 得 attrahere，其名词 attractio 衍生英语 attraction。

items.example: The verb is the physical core of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整族词的物理核心。

items.example: The prefix turns a pull into a pull toward a center.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「拉」变成「朝一个中心拉」。

items.example: The compound is the source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是英语名词的来源。

items.example: The Latin noun carries the action into English.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词把动作带进英语。

items.meaning: a pull toward; a thing that pulls
items.example: The English noun later names fairground draws and tourist sites.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语名词后来指游乐项目和旅游景点。

items.example: The verb is the plain action behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是名词背后的直白动作。

items.example: The suffix turns the action into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动作变成一种性质。

items.example: The same verb appears in the grip of a wheel.
items.exampleCN: 同一个动词出现在车轮的抓地力上。

items.example: The prefix reverses the direction of the pull.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把拉的方向反过来。

definition_en: the force that pushes things apart, or a strong feeling of dislike that pushes someone away
core_image: 两块同极磁铁靠近，中间的缝隙像有只看不见的手把它们往两边推开
scene: 他端起那碗搁久的汤，闻到气味就把碗推远，连筷子都不愿碰。The smell filled him with repulsion.
sceneCN: 这里 repulsion 指闻到某物后从心里涌起的强烈厌恶（第 5 个义项：强烈的反感）；句意为那股气味使他满心厌恶。图中可辨识物件：汤碗、推远的手、放下的筷子、皱起的鼻子。

pos.zh: 排斥；斥力；厌恶；反感

senses.title: The act of driving something back
senses.definition: the action of forcing an approaching person, army or object to turn back
senses.definitionCN: 迫使靠近的人、军队或物体退回去的动作
senses.example: The repulsion of the raid cost the attackers dearly.
senses.exampleCN: 这次击退突袭让进攻方付出惨重代价。
senses.why: Latin repellere joined re- 'back' to pellere 'to drive', so repulsion is literally a driving back.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 repellere 以 re-「回」加 pellere「推、驱动」，所以 repulsion 字面上就是「往回赶」。

senses.title: A force that pushes bodies apart
senses.definition: a physical force that makes two bodies move away from each other
senses.definitionCN: 使两个物体相互远离的物理力
senses.example: The repulsion between the two charges grew as they were brought closer.
senses.exampleCN: 两个电荷越靠近，它们之间的斥力越大。
senses.why: Two bodies that will not approach behave as if an invisible hand drives each away, which is the old verb in physics.
senses.whyCN: 两个不肯靠近的物体，就像有只看不见的手把它们各自赶开，这正是那个老动词在物理学里的用法。

senses.title: Electrostatic repulsion
senses.titleCN: 同种电荷之间的静电斥力
senses.definition: the push between electric charges of the same sign
senses.definitionCN: 同种电荷之间的推拒
senses.example: Electrostatic repulsion keeps the two wires from touching.
senses.exampleCN: 静电斥力使两根导线不相接触。
senses.why: Like charges refuse to share the same space, and the driving-back image fits that refusal exactly.
senses.whyCN: 同种电荷不肯占据同一处空间，「往回赶」的画面恰好贴合这种拒绝。

senses.title: Magnetic repulsion
senses.definition: the push between magnetic poles of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 同类磁极之间的推拒
senses.example: The repulsion between like poles levitated the small train.
senses.exampleCN: 同极之间的排斥使那列小车悬浮起来。
senses.why: A magnet is the most visible place where two objects refuse to meet, so the word settles there too.
senses.whyCN: 磁体是两物拒绝相遇最直观的地方，这个词也因此在那里落脚。

senses.title: Strong dislike or disgust
senses.definition: a feeling of disgust that makes a person want to move away from something
senses.definitionCN: 使人想远离某物的强烈厌恶感
senses.example: The smell filled him with repulsion.
senses.exampleCN: 那股气味使他满心厌恶。
senses.why: Disgust is felt as a push away from the object, the same outward motion as physical repulsion, and the metaphor was fixed by the eighteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 厌恶被感觉成一股把人与物推开的力，与物理排斥同为向外的运动，这一比喻在十八世纪固定下来。

senses.title: The quality of being repugnant
senses.titleCN: 事物本身令人反感的性质
senses.definition: the quality in something that makes people recoil from it
senses.definitionCN: 某物使人退缩、避开的性质
senses.example: A quiet repulsion hung about the empty house.
senses.exampleCN: 那座空屋笼罩着一种无声的排斥感。
senses.why: The word can name not only the feeling but the thing that produces it, since the object seems to push people away by itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不仅指感受，也指产生感受的事物，因为那东西仿佛自己在把人推开。

senses.title: A rebuff or rejection
senses.definition: a sharp refusal of an offer, an advance or a request
senses.definitionCN: 对提议、示好或请求的断然拒绝
senses.example: Her repulsion of his offer ended the negotiation.
senses.exampleCN: 她对他提议的回绝终结了谈判。
senses.why: To reject a request is to drive the asker back, so the physical verb serves for social refusal.
senses.whyCN: 拒绝一个请求就是把提出者推回去，于是这个物理动词也用于社交上的回绝。

senses.title: Mutual avoidance between groups
senses.titleCN: 群体或观念之间的相互排斥
senses.definition: a settled dislike that keeps two groups or ideas apart
senses.definitionCN: 使两个群体或观念保持距离的持久反感
senses.example: The repulsion between the two factions made any coalition impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 两个派系之间的相互排斥使任何联合都不可能。
senses.why: Groups that will not mix behave like like poles, and the word extends from bodies to collective identities.
senses.whyCN: 不肯混合的群体就像同极磁体，这个词便从物体扩展到集体身份。

intro.en: Repulsion comes from late Latin repulsio, from repellere 'to drive back', built on re- 'back' and pellere 'to push, drive'. It is not related to the noun pulse.
intro.cn: repulsion 来自晚期拉丁 repulsio，出自 repellere「推回、击退」，由 re-「回」加 pellere「推、驱动」构成；它与名词 pulse 不同源。

items.en: Pellere meant to push, strike or drive a thing before one, the physical act behind the whole family.
items.cn: pellere 意为推、击、把东西赶到前面，是整族词背后的物理动作。

items.en: The prefix re- meant back or again, so the compound verb described driving an attacker back.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 意为「回、再」，因此这个复合动词指把进攻者赶回去。

items.en: Repellere meant to drive back, repel an attack, or reject a demand; its noun repulsio named that driving back.
items.cn: repellere 意为推回、击退进攻或回绝要求；其名词 repulsio 指这种「赶回」。

items.en: The noun entered English through French, first of military and physical driving back.
items.cn: 这个名词经法语进入英语，最初用于军事与物理上的推回。

items.en: Physics gave the word to forces that make bodies separate, first in magnetism and then in electricity.
items.cn: 物理学把这个词赋予使物体分离的力，先用于磁，再用于电。

items.en: The exact first dates for the emotional sense are approximate; the Latin noun and verb are well attested.
items.cn: 情感义的确切首见年代为约数；这个拉丁名词与动词都有充分记录。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like repulsion; the second group names neighbouring kinds of disgust and rejection.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 repulsion 相近；第二组是意思相邻的其他「厌恶、拒绝」说法。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to drive back or to make someone feel disgust; it is the action behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 意为击退或使人厌恶的动词；它是名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning causing disgust or pushing away; it describes the effect, not the force itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为令人厌恶或排斥的形容词；描述效果，而非力本身。

entries.definition: The act of driving something forward; the prefix pro- means forward, the opposite of the back in repulsion.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物向前推进；前缀 pro- 意为「向前」，与 repulsion 中的「回」相反。

entries.definition: A sudden strong disgust; it comes from Latin revellere 'to tear away', a different root, and only looks like repulsion.
entries.definitionCN: 指突然的强烈厌恶；来自拉丁 revellere「撕裂、扯开」，与 repulsion 不同源，只是形近。

entries.definition: The edible seed of a legume; that word comes from Latin puls 'porridge', not from the verb that gave repulsion.
entries.definitionCN: 指豆类的可食种子；这个词来自拉丁 puls「粥」，并非出自产生 repulsion 的那个动词。

entries.definition: A strong feeling of dislike caused by something offensive to the senses or the morals.
entries.definitionCN: 指由触犯感官或道德的事物引起的强烈厌恶。

entries.definition: A settled dislike that makes one turn away from something.
entries.definitionCN: 指使人避开某物的持久反感。

entries.definition: A milder dislike, often of a flavor, manner or topic.
entries.definitionCN: 指较轻的厌恶，常针对味道、举止或话题。

entries.definition: The act of refusing an offer or a person; it names the refusal, not the feeling that pushes away.
entries.definitionCN: 指对提议或人的拒绝；它指回绝行为，而非推开的感觉。

entries.definition: The power of a substance to keep insects or other creatures away.
entries.definitionCN: 指某物质驱开昆虫或其他生物的性质。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin root, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Pellere is Latin for to drive or push, and re- means back, so repulsion is a driving back.
normal.cn: pellere 是拉丁语「推、赶」，re- 意为「回」，所以 repulsion 就是「往回赶」。

normal.en: The family runs repel, repulsive, repulsively and repulsiveness, and propulsion shares the same verb.
normal.cn: 同族词有 repel、repulsive、repulsively 与 repulsiveness，而 propulsion 共用同一个动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the everyday sense: mutual repulsion, electrostatic repulsion, a feeling of repulsion.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出日常义：相互排斥、静电斥力、厌恶感。

normal.en: In physics, repulsion is the opposite of attraction: one pushes apart, the other pulls together.
normal.cn: 物理学中 repulsion 的反面是 attraction：一个把物体推开，一个把物体拉近。

normal.en: Pulse is not related: the edible seed comes from Latin puls 'porridge', a different word entirely.
normal.cn: pulse 与它无关：指豆类种子的那个词来自拉丁 puls「粥」，完全是另一个词。

abstract.en: Picture two like poles meeting and a gap opening between them without anyone touching them.
abstract.cn: 想象两个同极靠近，没人碰它们，中间却裂开一道缝。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing a plate away the moment a bad smell reaches the nose.
abstract.cn: 想象气味一冲到鼻子，一只手立刻把盘子推开。

abstract.en: Picture two groups at one table who will not pass anything to each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两群人围坐一桌，却什么也不肯递给对方。

examples.en: The magnetic repulsion was strong enough to keep the rotor centered.
examples.cn: 磁斥力强到足以让转子保持居中。

examples.en: The study measured public repulsion toward the new tax.
examples.cn: 这项研究测量了公众对新税的反感程度。

examples.en: Her repulsion of the proposal surprised the whole committee.
examples.cn: 她对提案的回绝让整个委员会感到意外。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞怕个身」——一闻就怕，赶紧把身子挪开

root: 拉丁 pellere「推、驱动」→ 加 re-「回」成 repellere「推回、击退」→ 晚期拉丁 repulsio「赶回」→ 英语 repulsion；与 pulse 不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one push outward: an attack is driven back, like poles refuse each other, a smell drives a person away, and a request or a group is kept at a distance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一次向外推：进攻被赶回，同极相互拒绝，气味把人推开，请求或群体也被挡在远处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two like magnetic poles come close and an invisible hand pushes them apart.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个同极磁体靠近，一只看不见的手把它们往两边推开。

branches.en: THE OLD ACT: to drive back an attacker or a demand is the plain military origin of the word.
branches.cn: 古老的动作：把进攻者或要求赶回去，是这个词朴素的军事来源。

branches.en: THE FORCE NAMED: bodies that will not approach behave as if driven apart.
branches.cn: 被命名的力：不肯靠近的物体，行为就像被赶开。

branches.en: TWO FIELDS: electric charges and magnetic poles are where the push outward is easiest to see.
branches.cn: 两个领域：电荷与磁极是向外推最容易被看见的地方。

branches.en: DISGUST AND ITS OBJECT: a smell or a sight is felt as a push away, and the thing itself seems to do the pushing.
branches.cn: 厌恶与其对象：气味或景象被感觉成一股推开的力，而那东西仿佛自己在推。

branches.en: SOCIAL PUSHES: an offer is rebuffed, and two groups stay apart like like poles.
branches.cn: 社交上的推：提议被回绝，两个群体像同极一样保持距离。

intro.en: Repulsion is built from a Latin verb for driving and a prefix meaning back, and the same verb supports several English words.
intro.cn: repulsion 由一个表示「驱赶」的拉丁动词和一个表示「回」的前缀构成，这个动词还支撑起若干英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pellere gives repel, repulsion, repulsive and propulsion; pulse is a different word and is not part of this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pellere 衍生 repel（击退）、repulsion（排斥）、repulsive（令人厌恶的）与 propulsion（推进）；pulse 是另一个词，不属于这一族。

items.example: The verb is the physical push behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整族词背后的物理推力。

items.example: The prefix turns the push into a push backward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把推变成往回推。

items.example: The compound verb is the source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合动词是英语名词的来源。

items.example: The late Latin noun carries the action into English.
items.exampleCN: 这个晚期拉丁名词把动作带进英语。

items.meaning: a driving back; a force apart
items.example: Physics later gives the noun its force sense.
items.exampleCN: 物理学后来给这个名词赋予了力的含义。

items.example: The verb keeps the plain action of pushing away.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词保留「推开」的直白动作。

items.example: The suffix makes a quality out of the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动作变成一种性质。

items.example: The prefix reverses the direction of the same verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把同一个动词的方向反过来。

items.example: The ending names the thing that does the pushing.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾指做出推赶动作的事物。
